At least five trees were down in the Pilgrim Mill area, with one of these trees down on a home and another down on a vehicle.  Several of the downed trees also impacted power lines.  Trees were down on power lines on Holtzclaw Road, Tanglewood Drive, Shady Grove Road, and Jensen Trail and along Pilgrim Mill Road.

The Sumter County Emergency Management Director reported that four pecan trees were down in a pecan orchard.  Several large tree branches were also down in the orchard as well on other trees.  One nearby building had damaged shingles.
Fox 5 Television of Atlanta relayed a report from a viewer of quarter-sized hail near Cleveland.  A separate report of penny-sized hail was received from the public in the Cleveland area as well.

The Clarke County 911 Center reported that at approximately six trees were down across the far eastern part of the county, mostly in the Winterville area and near the Oglethorpe county line.  Trees were down on Danielsvlle Road, Freeman Drive, and near the intersection of North Church Road and Smokey Road.  At least two power lines were also down.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees were blown down from strong winds caused by thunderstorm outflow well north of the actual thunderstorms across the southern part of the county and counties immediately to the south.  The trees also brought down a power line which ignited a small wildfire.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a 14-year old male was struck by lightning while standing outside his home in the Huntington Ridge subdivision in McDonough.  The boy died overnight in the hospital following the incident.  A 15-year old girl was simultaneously injured by the same lightning strike, but survived and was said to be in good condition the next day.

CBS Atlanta reported that a 14-year old boy was struck by lightning during an afternoon thunderstorm while taking shelter under a tree adjacent to Lake Acworth.  The boy was taken to the hospital after being administered CPR by one of his friends.  The lightning was said to have struck his lower back and then traveled through his body coming out of his ear and the top of his shoulder blades.  He had to be revived three times as he was not breathing and had no pulse after the lightning strike.
A storm spotter observed penny-sized hail in downtown Woodstock.
The public reports that a few trees and large tree limbs were down along House Road in north Fulton county near Roswell.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that a commercial building was struck by lightning.  No specific damage details were provided.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that an apartment building was struck by lightning.  No specific damage details were provided.

The public observed quarter-sized hail near Cartersville ranging up to golf ball-sized hail near and just south of Emerson near the Cobb county bordern.  Penny-sized hail was also observed by the public just before this time frame in the White area northeast of Cartersville.

The Times Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck an outbuilding on Jack Russell Road just off Mount Carmel Road in the Welcome community of western Coweta county.  The structure and all of its contents were a total loss from the resulting fire.

The Times Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck a home on Murphy Road in the Welcome community of western Coweta county.  Damages to the home were apparently minor.  However, a 27-year old female inside the home was apparently injured by the lightning as she was having difficulty breathing following the incident and was transported to an Atlanta hospital.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck the attic of a home on Goldfield Trace in the Forest Plantation subdivision.  The attic suffered significant damage from the resulting fire.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck two trees behond a home on Old Peachtree Road.  The trees fell against a 16 by 20 foot shed which then caught fire.  The shed was destroyed from the fire.
The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a storage shed outside of a home on Charleston Oak Circle.  The shed was destroyed from the resulting fire.
The News Daily of Jonesboro reported that lightning struck a home on Fieldgreen Drive.  The resulting fire to the attic caused extensive damage to the home.
The News Daily of Jonesboro reported that lightning struck a second home in Jonesboro, this time on Elliot Drive.  The home suffered significant damage from the resulting fire.
The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a town home on Summit Cove Drive causing extensive damage to the two-story unit.

The Talbotton New Era reported that a thunderstorm downburst blew down the brick front wall of the remains of an old building in downtown Talbotton at the intersection of Washington Avenue and Monroe Street.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Towne Village Drive just north of Duluth.  The fire spread very quickly and the home was completely destroyed.  Even the home next door was threatened by the fire until firefighters could get the situation under control.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a building at the Sugarloaf Apartments on Meadow Church Road just east of Duluth.  Although firefighters were able to contain the resulting fire to the attic of the three-story building, six of the apartments suffered heavy smoke and water damage.  Several residents were displaced as a result of the fire.

The Forsyth County News reported that three male teenagers were struck and injured by lightning just off Jot-Em-Down Road northeast of Cumming.  The teenagers had just finished riding motorcycles off-road when the incident occurred.  One of the teenagers, a 14-year old, was hospitalized as a result of the injuries sustained.
The Rome News Tribune reported that two homes and vehicle on Virginia Circle, near the Coosa Country Club, were damaged when lightning struck an adjacent tree causing it to fall.
The Rome News Tribune reported that lightning struck a tree adjacent to a home on Brookwood Avenue in northwest Rome.  The tree fell on the home causing the laundry room to cave in.
The Macon Telegraph reported that lightning struck a home on Echeconnee Lane north of Centerville.  The resulting fire was confined to the utility room.

The Milton Herald reported that a large mansion home on Tullgean Drive was completely destroyed by a lightning strike.  A firefighter was injured while fighting the fire when the roof collapsed on him.  He suffered first and second degree burns on his legs.
The Milton Herald reported that a second home was struck by lightning in Milton, this time in the Oxford Lake subdivision.  Damage to this home was confined to the roof and two rooms.
The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a home on Silvertop Drive resulting in minor damage to the structure.  No specific details were provided.
The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a home on Mitford Lane.  The home suffered extensive damage from fire and smoke.
The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Biltmore Woods Drive just east of Buford.  The resulting fire was contained to an exterior wall.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Sydney Crest Lane.  The resulting fire caused moderate damage to an exterior wall and the attic.  The entire home suffered extensive smoke damage.  The fire appeared to start when the lightning struck the incoming electrical line to the home.  The family of four was displaced as a result of the incident.

A storm spotter reported that two large pine trees were snapped, numerous large branches were down, and more than 50 percent of the shingles were peeled from a home's roof.  The spotter estimated that wind gusts were 60 mph or greater.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that 15 to 20 trees were blown down near or along Georgia Highway 282 between Ellijay and Tails Creek near the Murray county line.  The roof and a garage door of an Ellijay fire station suffered minor damage.
The Harris County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were blown down around the county.  Trees were down on Georgia Highway 116, Macedonia Road, Trammell Mill Road, and Coal Springs Road.
The public reported that several trees and power lines were down in the east central portion of the county, near Woodbury.
The public observed penny-sized hail near Woodbury.
The Bartow County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down around Cartersville.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that at least five trees and one power line were down from the north central part of the county near Waleska to Canton in the central part of the county.  The power line was down southwest of Canton along Bells Ferry Road.  A wind gust of 59 mph was measured on weather equipment located at the Emergency Operations Center in Canton.

The Cobb County 911 Center reported widespread and extensive damage from downed trees across the southern portion of the county, from Powder Springs, to Austell, to Mableton.  Several of the trees fell on homes and a number of power lines were also brought down as well.  Over 1000 residents in the county were left without power following the storms, in some cases throughout the night.
The public observed quarter-sized hail in the Hiram area.

The Douglas County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were blown down around Chapel Hill.  Trees were down on Holland Drive, Central Church Road, and North Shelby Lane.  Three trees were down on a home and three vehicles on North Shelby Road.  Several power lines were also down across the city and many power outages were reported in the area.  At least 1500 people in the county were left without power for several hours.
The Telfair County 911 Center reported that three trees were blown down between the Dodge county border and Jacksonville, near Georgia Highway 117.
The Wheeler County 911 Center reported that three trees were down on U.S. Highway 441 near and south of Little Ocmulgee State Park in the far western part of the county, near the Telfair county line.
The Monroe County 911 Center reported that four trees were down in the southeast part of the county, southeast of Forsyth.
The Fayette County 911 Center reported that a number of trees and power lines were down across the northern portion of the county from north of Peachtree City to northwest of Fayetteville.

The Henry County 911 Center reported that many trees and power lines were down throughout a recreational vehicle (RV) park located along Jodico Road approximately 3 miles west-northwest of McDonough.  Several trees were also down along Interstate-75 from exits 218 to 222.

The Jasper County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down across the southwest part of the county.  One power pole was broken in half as well.  One tree fell on a vehicle.  Most of the damage was along Partridge Drive, Cook Road, and Pine Tree Road.

The Sumter County 911 Center reported that two trees were down on power lines in the north part of the county, north of Americus near the Schley county border.  U.S. Highway 27 was temporarily blocked from a downed tree.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that lightning struck a home in the Marietta Country Club neighborhood near Kennesaw.  No specific details were provided regarding the fire.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a second home, also in the Marietta Country Club neighborhood near Kennesaw, was struck by lightning.  Again, no specific details were provided regarding the resulting fire.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that yet a third home near Kennesaw was struck and set on fire by lightning.  This home was located on Stilesboro Drive.  Again, no specific details were provided regrading damages to the home.

The public reported that well over a dozen trees were snapped off approximately 15 feet above the ground or uprooted in eastern and southeast Paulding county.  Most of the downed or damaged trees were in the Morningside Drive, Morris Road, South Lake Drive, Harper's Lake Drive, and Cleburne Parkway areas.  Public estimated that the damage was the result of a thunderstorm downburst.

The Haralson County Emergency Management Director and the county 911 Center reported that three trees were down across the southern part of the county.  A couple of phone lines were also down as a result.

WXIA Television of Atlanta reported that two teenage girls were struck by lightning while standing under a tree adjacent to their home at the Windwood apartments, just south of Mableton.  The 16-year old female died shortly after being transported from the scene to the hospital.  Her 14-year old cousin died on July 21st after being hospitalized in critical condition and on a respirator since the lightning strike on the 13th.

The Bibb County Emergency Management Agency reported that over two dozen trees were down from the northwest part of the county, north and northwest of Lake Tobesofkee southeast across the county to south and south-southeast of Macon.  At least a dozen trees were down within the city of Macon as well.  A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 62 mph one mile south of the intersection of Eisenhower Parkway and Pio Nono Avenue, approximately one mile south of downtown Macon.

The Newnan Times-Herald reported that strong thunderstorm wind gusts blew down a large 100-year old oak tree onto the right front corner of a Coweta county school building near Newnan.  The downed tree caused damage to the metal roof, guttering, and minor damage to the conrete roof support underneath.  The Newnan fire department reported that they received over two dozen calls of downed trees and power lines around Newnan from the afternoon storms.

Fox 5 Television of Atlanta and the Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a home on Roberts Street just northeast of Buford.  The single story, single family home was completely destroyed as a result of the ensuing fire.  A family of four was displaced as a result of this incident, but no injuries occurred.

The USGS stream gage on Big Creek near Cumming (CMMG1) exceeded its flood stage of 6.0 feet at 1030 pm EDT.  The river continued to rise and reached 8.14 feet at 515 am EDT on July 17, 2010.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal adjacent to the creek.
The Bartow County Emergency Management Director reported that at least nine trees were down around Cartersville, some on power lines.

Fox 5 Television of Atlanta, along with other Atlanta broadcast media and the Cartersville Daily Tribune reported that heavy rain flooded several downtown Cartersville businesses as well as causing a partial roof collapse of the Hobby Lobby store at the Market Square Shopping Center.  Three to four inches of rain had fallen in a small area around downtown Cartersville during the previous two hours.  Considerable damage was reported to the store building and its contents, many of which were destroyed by rain water.  However, no injuries were reported as a result of the incident.||Several other downtown businesses suffered water damage when several inches of water crept into the structures, including Four Way Lunch, Swheat Market, City Cellar, and Moore's Market.  Several nearby homes on Herring Street were flooded with 2.5 to 3.0 feet of water.  Seven residents of these homes were rescued from the flooded homes.  Finally, the Keith Building, a city building, on Leake Street sustained significant water damage when water rose nearly two feet deep in the lower level of the structure.  Minor flooding was also observed at the building housing the Cartersville Daily Tribune.||Most of the flooding was determined to be the result of a clogged drainage ditch near the CSX Railroad tracks.  This prevented the heavy runoff water from reaching the nearby Etowah River.

The Murray County 911 Center reported that thunderstorm downburst winds blew down at least six trees southwest of Chatsworth near the intersection of Georgia Highway 225 and New Hope Church Road.  In addition, a portion of the roof of a home was ripped off.  Several large tree limbs were also down, falling on and causing damage to some vehicles.

The Douglas County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the county from thunderstorm winds.  The trees were down on Wallace Lake Road, Beaver Lake Road, and Mann Road at the railroad crossing.  The tree down on Wallace Lake Road was also on a power line.  The public measured wind gusts at 43 mph during this thunderstorm in the Douglasville area.

The Douglas County Emergency Manager, the Atlanta broadcast media, and the Douglas County Sentinel reported that a 15-year old male was struck by lightning while working with his father in the garage at their home on Bellemeade Drive off Coursey Lake Road.  The teenage boy was apparently pushing the garage door opener button to close the door when the lightning strike occurred.  The boy's arm was numb for several hours, but otherwise all injuries appeared to be minor.  He was transported to a local hospital, treated, and released.
The Douglas County 911 Center reported that a tree on Bomar Road at Berry Farm Road was struck by lightning causing it to fall onto a power line.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that approximately six trees and a couple of power lines were down around Wrightsville, especially on the north and west side of the city.  Trees were down on Oilver Road southwest of the city.
The Spalding County 911 Center reported that two trees were down on the east side of Griffin.  One tree fell on a home causing damage to the structure.  The other tree fell on a power line.
An amateur radio operator reported that a tree was down across a road and a power lines near McCollum Road and Georgia Highway 54, near Hampton.

The Macon Telegraph reported that an elderly couple passed away at their home of 62-years as the result of heat exposure or heat exhaustion.  The 90-year old male and 83-year old female couple left their home around 1030 am EDT Friday, 07/23/10, to go outside to a wooded area behind their home, approximately 50 yards away from the house.  They were both found dead by their son approximately 24 hours later still adjacent to their vehicle were they had gone the previous morning to discard some kitchen scraps.

A storm spotter reported that four 10-12 inch diameter trees were blown down or snapped-in-half along Moon Station Lane Northwest near Acworth.  It was also reported that several tree limbs and associated debris were scattered about the area.  WSB Television of Atlanta reported that another tree was blown down onto a home along Hickory Creek Court in Acworth.  The downed tree caused damage to the chimney and gutters as well as an adjacent Fence.

The Bartow County 911 Center relayed reports of nickel to golf ball-sized hail from the northwest part of the county between Adairsville and the Floyd and Gordon county lines.  The large hail broke windows of homes in Adairsville.  A couple of trees were also down from thunderstorms winds.  One tree was down on Jarrett Loop Road and another on White Road.
The Chattooga County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were down.  At least one power line was down with power outages noted in Summerville.

The Floyd County 911 Center and the public works department reported that at least four trees were down across the northern portion of the county.  The downed trees were causing blockage on Jones Mill, Buttrum, and Mountain Roads north of Rome.

The Fannin County 911 Center reported that four trees were down from west of Blue Ridge to near Mineral Bluff.  The trees were down on Blackberry Drive, Sugar Creek Road, Scenic Drive, and Cutcane Road.
The Fannin County 911 Center reported that a lightning strike caused damage to their emergency service radio just outside of Morganton.

A cluster of thunderstorms developed across central Coweta county shortly just after midnight on July 25th and persisted around Newnan for two to three hours.  Three to four inches of rain fell in this area during this time frame resulting in flash flooding and flooding of streets and property.  Flash flooding was observed along several roads around Newnan, including McCullom-Sharpsburg Road/Georgia Highway 154, Thomason Road, East Broad Street, Jefferson Street, and Postal Parkway.  Walt Sanders Road, just off Georgia Highway 34, was closed with one to two feet of water over it as well.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal in the flooded areas.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a 47-year old female of Jeffersonville passed away from heat exposure.  She was found sitting on her unshaded porch outside her home.  The temperature in the area that day was already 99 degrees at noon.  Subsequent medical examination determined that the individual died from a cardiac event, induced by the intense heat.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that a large tree had fallen on a home on Stanley Parkway, approximately six miles northwest of Ringgold.  Considerable damage was noted to the structure.  Pea-sized hail was also observed in the area.

The Dawson County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees were blown down along Old Savannah Place off Thompson Road.  One of the trees fell on a trailer causing significant damage to the trailer and injuring a woman inside.

The public observed penny to nickel-sized hail in the southeast part of the county, four to five miles south of Nicholson.  Two trees were also blown down near the intersection of U.S. Highway 441 and Georgia Highway 334.
The public observed penny-sized hail from southeast of Duluth northwest to near the Fulton county line.  Hail was observed on Pleasant Hill and Club Drive southeast of Duluth.
The public observed quarter-sized hail in the far southern part of the county along the Fulton county line near and southeast of Brookwood.

The public observed quarter to half-dollar-sized hail from the Johns Creek area to the east side of Alpharetta.  One tree was also blown down near the intersection of Pine Lake Drive and Merlendale Drive, just south-southwest of Sandy Springs.

The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported that several power lines were down near Rockbridge Road and Lawrenceville Highway near Lilburn.  A large tree fell on a vehicle at the entrance to the Idlewylde Apartments on Boggs Road in Duluth.  The adult male inside was pinned in the vehicle and had to be extricated by fire officials.  Two power lines were also down on South Old Peachtree Road just east-northeast of Duluth.  At least one tree was also down on Princess South, just northeast of Lilburn.

The Floyd County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in Rome, one tree was down in Lindale, and another tree was down in Cave Spring during a 30-minute time frame from 500 pm to 530 pm EDT.  Two trees were down at the intersection of Horseleg and River Streets and another tree was down on Crane Street in Rome.

The Cobb County 911 Center reported that several trees and a few power lines were blown down in the northeast part of the county in the Roswell Road area.  The public measured a wind gust of 63 mph in the Oakdale and Rose Garden subdivisions.

The USGS stream gage on Sweetwater Creek at Club Drive (STWG1) reached its flood stage of 11.0 feet at 730 pm EDT.  The creek remained in flood until 935 pm EDT.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal near the creek.
The Houston County 911 Center reported that five trees were blown down around the city of Warner Robins.
The Baldwin County 911 Center reported that three trees were blown down near Underwood.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that a one-story business was struck and set on fire by lightning on Howell Street in Duluth.  The attic suffered extensive damage from the fire.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that a lightning strike to an apartment on Concepts Drive in Norcross resulted in minor smoke damage to the structure.  No fire was observed upon arrival by the firefighters.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck the electrical line of a home on Ivy Park Lane in Norcross.  The lightning strike traveled through the dryer vent into the house.  Firefighters found heavy smoke in the structure upon arrival, but no fire.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a two-story wood frame home on Mill Bend Drive in Lawrenceville.  Firefighters found the attic and a bedroom on fire when they arrived.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that a two-story house on Meadow Point Drive was heavily involved in a lightning-related fire when firefighters arrived.  The house was a total loss.  The fire was so intense that the adjacent home also suffered moderate siding damage.

A cluster of thunderstorms developed across central Coweta county shortly just after midnight on July 25th and persisted around Newnan for two to three hours.  Three to four inches of rain fell in this area during this time frame resulting in flash flooding and flooding of streets and property.  Shenadoah Boulevard near the White Oak Golf Course was flooded with up to four feet of water flowing over the road.  Several other roads in the area were flooded with up to two feet of water over some of these as well.  A resident of Newnan reported that water was two feet deep in his yard on Prestwick Drive.  Flash flooding was observed along McCullom-Sharpsburg Road or Georgia Highway 154, Thomason Road, East Broad Street, Jefferson Street, and Postal Parkway.  Walt Sanders Road, just off Georgia Highway 34, was closed with one to two feet of water over it as well.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal in the flooded areas.
The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home on Paisley Court in Lilburn.  The resulting fire destroyed the single-story wood-frame home.
The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that a single-story wood-frame home was struck by lightning on Buford Highway in Duluth.  The home was destroyed from the resulting fire.

The Carroll County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees and power lines were blown down in the southern part of the county, mostly southeast of Bowdon.  A few trees and tree limbs were also down in and around Carrollton.  A barn just southeast of Bowdon lost parts of its roof from strong thunderstorm wind gusts.
The Telfair County 911 Center relayed a report of penny-sized hail in the area.
The Telfair County 911 Center reported that a few trees were down in McRae and near the county 911 center at 185 East Oak Street.
The Wheeler County 911 Center reported that a few trees were down near the western border of the county, especially in the Spring Hill area.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a double lightning bolt struck a 66-acre farm just north of Jasper killing four thoroughbred horses valued over $100,000.  The lightning bolts apparently hit the pasture where the horses were grazing and traveled through a drainage pipe that ran underneath a dam where the horses were standing at the time of the incident.

The Laurens County Emergency Management Director reported that up to 10 trees were down across the county.  Most of the trees were down across the southern half of the county from Dexter to Rentz.  A few trees were also down in East Dublin.
The Dodge County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees and one power line were down near Eastman.
The Jackson County Fire Department observed quarter-sized hail at the intersection of Georgia Highway 60 and New Cut Road near Brasleton.
The Walton County 911 Center reported that at least a dozen trees were down across the eastern portion of the county.

The Morgan County 911 Center reported that six to seven trees were down across the county, but mostly in the Buckhead community.  Trees were down near the intersection of Commerce Street and U.S. Highway 278.
The public reported that several trees were blown down around Eatonton.  A portion of U.S. 441 Business Highway in the city of Eatonton was closed.
The Warren County 911 Center reported that a lightning strike rendered the emergency center's radios inoperative for several hours.
The Hancock County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down near Shoulderbone.
The Sumter County Emergency Management Director reported that hail of penny, perhaps slightly larger, fell in the southwest part of the county near Croxton Crossroads.
The Sumter County Emergency Management Director reported that three trees and one power line were down between Croxton Crossroads and the west side of Americus.
The Rockdale Citizen of Conyers reported that a home on Costly Mill Road was struck and set on fire by lightning.  The home was completely destroyed.

The Times Georgian of Carrollton reported that lightning struck a propane tank at Lyle Enterprises near Carrollton.  The lightning strike caused an explosion which set a 2400 square foot workshop on fire.  This fire in turn set an adjacent mobile home, that was used for storage, four trucks, a tractor, some lawn mowers, and other miscellaneous supplies on fire.  All of this property was destroyed as a result.

The Griffin Daily News reported that lightning struck the McDonough Road Baptist Church located at 1370 North McDonough Road.  The lightning struck the front gable, setting the attic on fire.  The resulting fire caused severe damage to the attic, foyer, and roof.  The rest of the building suffered minor smoke and water damage.

The Leader Tribune of Peach County reported that lightning struck a home on Tucker Road near Byron.  The lightning strike put a large hole in the wall and set the structure on fire.  The home was subsequently completely destroyed.
The Daily Citizen of Dalton reported that a home on Robert Fuller Road in Tunnel Hill was struck by lightning.  The structure only sustained minimal damage from the incident.

The Marietta Daily Journal reported that lightning struck a home on Helga Way between Kennesaw and Woodstock in northeast Cobb county.  The home was severely damaged from the fire which took at least 30 minutes to contain.
The Barrow County 911 Center reported that five trees were down around Winder.
The Jackson County 911 Center reported that several power lines were down across the western part of the county.  One tree was also down.
The Peachtree City Fire Department reported that lightning struck a home on Spring Court off Rockaway Road, approximately three miles southeast of Peachtree City.  Damage to the structure was minor.
The public reported penny-sized hail around Fairplay on East Carroll Road.

The Douglas County Emergency Management Director reported that a home in Fairplay was struck by lightning.  Damage to the home was in the form of a damaged phone box and the electrical wiring adjacent to a clothes dryer in the utility room.

The Crisp County Emergency Management Director reported that a portion of a roof was blown off a home near Arabi and a barn, approximately three miles east of Georgia Veterans Memorial State Park, lost its roof in strong thunderstorm wind gusts.
The Bartow County 911 Center reported that at least six trees and a few power lines were down northwest of Cartersville, mostly in the Sugar Valley Road area.
The Bartow County 911 Center reported that seven homes across the county were struck by lightning.  Damages ranged from minor to moderate.
The Fannin County 911 Center reported that four trees were blown down across the eastern portion of the county, around Morganton on Old Georgia Highway 76.

The Murray County 911 Center reported that the roof was blown off a barn near the intersection of Maple Grove and Church Roads in the far southern part of the county, south of Ramhurst.  Three trees were also down in this same general area.
The Lumpkin County Emergency Management Director reported that four to five trees, mostly pine, were blown down.  At least one of these trees was dead and was partially blocking a road.
The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees were blown down in the far northeast part of the county.
The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees were blown down in the west central and central part of the county between Tails Creek and Ellijay.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees were blown down in the west central and northwest part of the county near Mountaintown.  Event times and location were based on radar data.  The Emergency Manager reported that approximately 10 trees were blown down across the county in an approximate one-hour period between 6 pm and 7 pm EDT.  Radar data suggests that much of this occurred near Tails Creek in the west central part of the county.
The DeKalb County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a tree causing the tree to split apart and fall.

The Douglas County Emergency Management Director reported that four lightning-related fires occurred across the county between 549 pm EDT and 601 pm EDT as strong thunderstorms tracked from northwest to southeast.

An off-duty employee with Warner Robins Air Force Base reported that lightning struck his home in Warner Robins.  While no fire was reported, damage was observed to electrical and telephone wiring and an air conditioning system.
The public observed half-dollar-sized hail in the Cooper Creek area in the far southeast part of Fannin county.
The public observed quarter-sized hail near Turners Corner.
The Wilcox County 911 Center reported that at least a dozen trees were down around Owensboro near Georgia Highway 233.

The Clarke County 911 Center reported that at least 10 trees and a half-a-dozen power lines were down from northwest of Winterville to south of Athens near the Oconee county line.  One tree was down on Simonton Bridge Road, blocking the road.

The Clarke County 911 Center reported that lightning set a commercial business on fire on Voyles Road, approximately two miles northwest of Winterville in northeast Clarke county.  The business suffered significant damage from the resulting fire.

The Clarke County 911 Center reported that lightning struck an apartment complex approximately three miles northeast of Athens on Rolling Ridge Drive.  Damage from the lightning-related fire was minor to moderate.
The Clarke County Emergency Management Director reported that a lightning strike caused minor damage to a home on Sing Tree Lane.
The Clarke County Emergency Management Director reported that a home on Danielsville Road suffered minor damage from a lightning strike.
The Clarke County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home on Old Pittard Road causing minor damage to the structure.

The Jackson County 911 Center reported that a portion of a roof was blown off one home and a chimney was blown off another home on Jameston Drive near Jefferson.  One tree was also down on Ralph Garrison Road.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that three commercial buildings in the John T. Pettit Drive area sustained roof damage.  One of the buildings lost nearly its entire roof.  The other two only sustained minor shingle damage.  Eight residential structures sustained minor damage.  The garage of one home suffered major damage when a large tree fell on the structure.  One vehicle was also destroyed by a large downed tree.  Dozens of large old hardwood trees were snapped off in the downtown Canton area, including several near Canton City Hall and on the grounds of the Board of Education Administrative Complex.  Many other small trees and tree limbs were also down in the area.  Widespread power outages were observed.  Much of the city of Canton was left without power.  The damage was the clearly the result of a pulse thunderstorm downburst.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that three homes in unincorporated Cherokee county were struck by lightning and sustained minor to moderate damage.  The public reported that a 60 foot live oak tree at the Department of Education building was struck by lightning.  The lightning strike caused the tree to fall on an adjacent Nissan Xterra, crushing the vehicle.

The Savannah Morning News reported that lightning struck the high school wing of the David Emanuel Academy near Stillmore in rural southeast Emanuel county.  The two-story building, which was constructed in 1904, was set on fire by the lightning strike and completely destroyed.  The fire destroyed a science lab, classroom, and wrestling gym.

The United States Forest Service reported flash flooding near the merging point of the Jacks River and the Conasauga River and several smaller creeks, streams, and tributaries.  Several campers and hikers were evacuated from the Alaculsy Valley Campground within the Cohutta Wildlife Management Agency.  Minor flooding was also observed along portions of Old Georgia Highway 2 and Cable Road to the west near Cisco.  Damage was confined to debris removal and minor erosion to a few secondary dirt roads.  The heavy rain and erosion also caused a few trees to fall on minor, secondary roads within the area.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported flash flooding along Byrd Creek, five miles north-northwest of Canton, and along Shoal Creek, one mile west-northwest of Waleska.  At least three feet of water from Byrd Creek was overflowing Sardis Circle north-northwest of Canton, and approximately a foot of water was flowing over George Gray Lane, just west-northwest of Waleska.  Minor erosion to the roads was observed, along with subsequent debris removal.

The White County Emergency Management Director reported significant flash flooding near and just south of Cleveland.  The most significant incident occurred along a service road of U.S. Highway 129, approximately one mile south of Cleveland.  Significant erosion, six to eight feet deep in spots, occurred in the area resulting in a pavement collapse.  The collapsed pavement resulted in a sink hole causing damage to a car wash and adjacent Sonic Drive In restaurant along U.S. Highway 129.  Most of the damage was in the form of collapsed awnings and damage to adjacent property at the drive in.  In addition, Cox Creek overflowed its banks onto U.S. Highway 129 near Campbell Street with four feet of water and onto Quillian Street with two feet of water.  Freeman Creek overflowed its banks onto Asbestos Road with one foot of water.  A secondary stream that flows into Cox Creek overflowed its banks flooding Cementary Street and Wildord Ash Parkway with one foot of water.  Portions of the Creekside Deli Parking Lot at Nachoochee Road and U.S. Highway 129 were also flooded.

The Athens Banner Herald reported that lightning struck a tree next to a home on State Street in Commerce.  The tree subsequently fell onto the roof of the adjacent garage, causing damage to the structure.

The Macon Telegraph reported that lightning struck a U.S. Postal Service mail carrier while placing mail in a mailbox on Rocky Creek Road in Macon.  The female mail carrier was taken to the hospital after asking for medical attention, but did not sustain any life-threatening injuries.
The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Woods River Lane in Duluth.  Firefighters were able to confine the fire to one wall, keeping damage to a minimum.

The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Hambrick Drive.  The lightning struck the attic area of the home.  The resulting fire caused extensive damage to the attic and moderate damage to the second floor of the home.

The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck the chimney of a home on Congress Parkway in Lawrenceville.  The chimney suffered moderate damage and a subsequent fire caused damage to the first and second floors of the home, mostly from smoke.

The Athens Banner Herald reported that lightning struck a home on W. H. Rayes Road near Jefferson.  The lightning strike caused damage to the electrical system of the home.  However, no fire was reported.
The Athens Banner Herald reported that lightning struck a home on Marshall Clark Road.  The gas line to the home was ignited, fueling a large fire at the scene.
The Jackson Progress Argus reported that lightning struck a home on Halls Bridge Road, which happened to be the home of the Butts county sheriff.  Only minor damage was reported to the structure.
The Jackson Progress Argus reported that lightning struck a home on First Street near downtown Jackson.  The structure sustained major fire and smoke damage as a result of the lightning strike.
The Athens Banner Herald reported that lightning struck a home on Antrim Glen Road.  The structure suffered moderate fire and smoke damage.

The Pickens and Cherokee County Emergency Management Directors report that a strong thunderstorm downburst had downed nearly 100 trees near the Cherokee county, near and just north of Tate.  At least nine power poles were also down, including one main power transmission line.  Several roads were blocked from downed trees.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that the same thunderstorm downburst that began just north of Nelson in Pickens county continued south into extreme northern Cherokee county before dissipating.  More than a dozen trees were down in the extreme northern part of the county north of Ball Ground, near the Pickens county line.

The Dooly County Emergency Management Director reported that a strong thunderstorm downburst downed 20 mature pecan trees and damaged another 30 mature pecan trees between Vienna and Byromville.  In addition, a 150-year old, six-foot diameter oak tree was blown down in the same thunderstorm wind gusts, falling on and destroying the porch of a home.  It was further noted that a field of corn was flattened by the strong winds.
The public observed quarter-sized hail near McDonough.
The public reported that several trees were down in and near Duluth, especially near the Chattahoochee River.

A storm spotter observed nickel to slightly larger than nickel-sized hail east of Loganville on Bay Creek Church Road.  The Walton County Emergency Management Director relayed several reports of pea-sized hail.  Radar data suggests that pea to nickel-size hail likely fell further west across the county as well, coincident with several reports of thunderstorm wind damage.

The Walton County Emergency Management Director reported that a tree was down on a home near Loganville, causing damage to the structure.  The Walton Electric Management Cooperative reported that a tree was down on a power line near Walnut Grove.  The public reported that two trees were down approximately five miles east of Loganville.  The downed trees broke a fence.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that a strong thunderstorm downburst, wind gusts of 60 mph or greater, blew down dozens of trees and several power lines from northeast of Wrightsville to three miles west-southwest of Wrightsville.  Six homes across this path sustained minor to moderate damage from downed trees.  Several trees were down and a trampoline was blown away from a residence near U.S. Highway 319 on Tucker Grove Church Road west of Wrightsville.

The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that five trees were blown down by a downburst from a small thunderstorm.  One of the trees fell on a home, just west of Rome, causing damage to the structure.

The La Grange Daily News reported that a large tree limb was blown from a tree during strong thunderstorm wind gusts causing it fall on a vehicle traveling on Broad Street near Springdale Street in La Grange.  Inside the vehicle were a mother and her three children.  Although none of the three children were injured, the mother had to be pulled from the vehicle and taken to a local hospital for surgery.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that eight to nine trees were down between Waleska and Ball Ground in the far northern portion of the county near the Pickens county line.
The Pickens County 911 Center reported that three trees and one power line were down in the far southern portion of the county between Talmadge and Tate near the Cherokee county line.
The public observed penny-sized hail near Smyrna.
The Troup County 911 Center reported that lightning ignited a small grass fire in a field near Baughs Crossroads in southern Troup county.

The Harris County Emergency Management Director reported that thunderstorm downburst winds blew over a chicken coop.  The winds also blew in the front and back doors of a nearby barn.  The doors were closed prior to the incident.
The public reported damage to a light fixture in a home caused by a lightning strike.  Other non-specific minor damage was also observed as a result of the lightning strike.

The Houston County Emergency Management Director reported that several roads from Warner Robins to Perry were flooded with several inches of water.  At least two roads had to be closed.  Two homes in Warner Robins were threatened by high water and were evacuated as a precaution.  Two retention ponds were found overflowing.  One home suffered minor flood damage in addition to debris removal from the flooded roads.
The Gilmer County 911 Center reported that a lightning strike caused a fire at the Gilmer County Water pump station in Ellijay.  One tree was also blown down in the area.

Several reports of hail, ranging in size from pennies to quarters, were received from the southeast and east central parts of Cobb county from just northwest of Mableton to just east of Smyrna.  Quarter-sized hail was observed near Mableton and Smyrna, with penny-sized hail just east of Smyrna.
The public observed golf ball-sized hail in the Sandy Springs area.
A deputy with the Meriwether County Sheriff's Office reported that several trees and power lines were down around Luthersville.

The Meriwether County Sheriff's Office reported that hail was observed near Luthersville.  Although a specific size was not specified, radar data across northern Meriwether county was analogous to several storms in neighboring counties that produced quarter or larger-sized hail.
A deputy with the Coweta County Sheriff's Office observed quarter-sized hail on Fischer Road between Thomas Crossroads and Cannongate.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director relayed reports of quarter-sized hail from the far northern part of the county near Salacoa Valley.
The public observed quarter-sized hail across northern Gwinnett county from the east side of Duluth to Hog Mountain.  Some accumulation was noted on the roadways.

The Laurens County Emergency Management Director reported that a weak and brief EF0 tornado touched down between Evergreen and Southern Belle Roads, just west of U.S. Highway 441, about 10 miles northwest of Dublin.  The tornado path length was estimated to only be 200 yards long with a maximum path width of 50 yards.  Twelve to 15 trees were down along the path of the tornado.  One of the downed trees destroyed an outbuilding and another caused minor damage to a home.  Radar data showed only a 40 dBZ shower in the area at the time on a tail end of much stronger activity across north central and east central Georgia.  No cloud-to-ground lightning was ever indicated in the shower that produced the tornado and the maximum cloud top on this cloud was below 20,000 feet.
The public observed quarter-sized hail approximately five miles south of Shady Dale in far east central Jasper county.

The Jasper County Sheriff's Office reported that five trees were down in the Monticello area, including one on Calvin Road, another on Jackson Lake Road, and one on Georgia Highway 83 going north toward Shady Dale.
The Putnam County 911 Center relayed reports of quarter-sized hail across the far northern part of the county.
The Putnam County 911 Center reported that four to five trees were blown down across the far northern part of the county near the Morgan county line.

The Morgan County Emergency Management Director reported that up to 15 trees were down across the county.  Trees were down in Rutledge, Madison, High Shoals, and Buckhead.  The Buckhead community suffered the most damage where one tree was down on a home and another was down on a vehicle.
The public observed penny-sized hail near Rutledge.
The Morgan County Emergency Management Director relayed a report of penny-sized hail from the Buckhead community.
The Jackson County 911 Center relayed a report of quarter-sized hail from the far northeastern part of the county in the Maysville area along the Banks county line.

The Jackson County 911 Center relayed a report of quarter-sized hail in the Maysville area long the Banks county line.  Radar data suggests that similar-size hail likely continued eastward toward Banks Crossing.
The public reported lots of pea to penny-sized hail in the Lithia Springs area.

The local electric management cooperative reported that three trees were down on power lines in the eastern part of the county, including one on Irwin Hill Road and another on Windy Hills Lane near Sonaraville.  Pea-sized hail was also observed in Calhoun.
The public observed quarter-sized hail south of Jonesboro and nickel-sized hail north of Jonesboro.

The Newton County Fire Department reported that four trees and one power line were down in the county.  Additional power lines were brought down by the downed trees.  A tree was down on a house and adjacent vehicle on Hale Drive, a tree was down on a power line on Emory Street and another was down on a power line on Cooper Road.  A tree was also down on Newton Ridge Road in the southern part of the county.  Power lines were down on Georgia Highway 142 near Fire Station No. 15.
The Butts County Emergency Management Director reported that a couple of power lines were down within the city of Jackson.

The Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech) police department and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a large oak tree fell on the Campus Christian Fellowship building near the intersection of Fourth Street and Techwood Drive.  The tree struck a transformer and a gas generator.  Several blocks of the campus were left without power.  Affected buildings included a dormitory and two fraternity houses.  These buildings were evacuated until repairs could be made.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Lyerly, south of Summerville, observed nickel-sized hail.  Radar data suggest that similar-size hail likely fell from here northeastward toward Summerville and Tidings.
The Gordon County 911 Center reported penny-sized hail near Calhoun.

The Citizen and Georgian of Montezuma reported that a large tree was blown down onto a home on Green Street during a strong thunderstorm.  The tree left a whole in the house about the size of a watermelon.  Considerable damage was noted to the roof, the attic, and the laundry room as a result.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported that a human-caused wildfire at South Dicks Ridge in Walker County burned 1/4 acre and caused $1000 in damages.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported a human-caused wildfire at South Dicks Ridge in Walker county.  The fire burned 1/4 acre and resulted in an estimated $1000 in damages.

A storm survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia, confirmed that an EF1 tornado, which began in DeKalb county Alabama, crossed into Dade county approximately two miles southwest of Rising Fawn.  The tornado then tracked east-northeast, lifting approximately two miles east of Rising Fawn near the eastern most extension of Holder Loop Road.  The maximum path width was determined to be 150 yards with maximum wind gusts estimated at 100 mph.  Considerable damage to trees and property was noted along the path of the tornado.  Thirty homes sustained minor roof damage either from the strong wind or downed trees.  Two barns were destroyed and a mobile home lost nearly all of its roof.  Nearly 200 trees were uprooted, snapped, or blown over along the path of the tornado.

The Walker County Emergency Management Director reported widespread downed trees and power lines throughout the county, but primarily the southern half, including LaFayette.  Nearly two dozen roads, including portions of Georgia Highways 341 and 136, were blocked from downed trees.  Consequently, several school districts had to delay their start time at least two hours.  An outbuilding at a private residence, where a number of antiques were stored, was destroyed when a large tree fell on the structure.  In addition, shingles were blown off roofs of homes on Shook Road and Old Bethel Roads.

A storm survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that strong straight-line winds, with gusts near 90 mph, had resulted in widespread downed trees in the northeast corner of the county between Morganville and Wildwood.  Much of the damage was along Mason and Lambert Roads.  Several homes sustained minor roof damage and two vehicles were also destroyed from downed trees.
The Chattooga County Emergency Management Director reported widespread damage to trees and power lines across the county.  Several buildings sustained roof damage from the winds and/or downed trees.
The Emergency Management Director reported quarter-sized hail across the northwest part of the county.

A storm survey conducted by the National Weather Service in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that an EF0 tornado had touched down approximately four miles northeast of Ringgold along Keiths Road.  The tornado traveled east-northeast for only 300 yards before lifting.  Maximum path width was determined to be 75 yards with maximum winds gusts estimated to be 80 mph.  Two homes, two chicken houses, and a barn suffered minor roof damage from the tornado.  In addition, approximately 50 trees were downed along the path of the tornado.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that a number of trees and power lines were down across the southern part of the county.  Several locations in the county, including Ringgold, were left without power.

The Whitfield County Emergency Management Director reported that a home on Alpison Road in Cohutta was destroyed when several large trees fell on the structure.  Amateur radio operators relayed reports that school buses encountered several downed trees and power outages.  The Whitfield County Emergency Management Director also reported that a few trees were down around Dalton with scattered power outages.
The Bartow County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down across the county.  In addition, one power line was down on a school bus.
The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down across the county.  One telephone pole was down across a road causing the road to be temporarily closed.

The public reported observing golf ball-sized hail near Resaca.  However, radar data was not supportive of hail this large.  The same storm only produced quarter-sized hail in Chattooga county and had already weakened by the time it reached Gordon county.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that six trees and a few power lines were down across the county.  Radar data suggests that the majority of this occurred from Ellijay westward as the line of thunderstorms weakened considerably as it moved into the eastern part of the county.
The Murray County Emergency Management Director reported that about six trees were down across the county, mainly in the Fort Mountain area.

The Haralson County Emergency Management Director reported that four trees were down across the county, mainly north of Georgia Highway 120.  A few power outages were also noted in the north part of the county.
The Fannin County 911 Center reported that more than half-a-dozen trees were down across the western part of the county.
The Paulding County Emergency Management Director reported that a structure in the northeast part of the county, just northeast of New Hope was destroyed by a lightning-related fire.
The Carroll County Emergency Management Director reported that three trees were down in the Carrollton vicinity.

The Douglas County 911 Center reported that a tree had fallen on a home causing considerable damage to the structure and trapping the family inside.  The family was rescued from the damaged home without incident or injury.
The Lumpkin County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the Porter Springs and Cavander Creek area approximately seven to eight miles northeast of Dahlonega.
The Union County 911 Center reported that six trees were down in the Track Rock, and Foyles Town areas in the east central and southeast part of the county.
The Fulton County 911 reported that there were three structure fires in the county caused by lightning.  No further information was provided.

Several reports of quarter to golf ball-sized hail were received from the public and amateur radio operators across the central part of Houston county from about halfway between Perry and Warner Robins to Kalthleen and Bonaire.  Hail was observed on both Georgia Highway 127 and Moody Road.  There was also one report of nickel-sized hail from the city of Perry, which likely fell around 240 pm EDT.
The Bleckley County Emergency Management Director reported nickel to quarter-sized hail east of Cochran.

The Laurens County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees and power lines were down in the East Dublin area, with a few more trees and power lines down east of East Dublin toward Brewton.  A home near Brewton suffered minor roof damage.  A barn in the same area also sustained moderate roof damage.  Downed trees were noted along U.S. Highway 319 and Ernest Road, east of East Dublin.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director relayed that numerous reports of quarter-sized hail were received from the south part of the county from north of Scott to Meeks and Kite, including the Moore's Chapel area.  Golf ball-sized hail was observed near Meeks and also on Georgia Highway 15 south of Wrightsville toward Meeks.  At least one home in the Meeks area sustained significant roof damage from the large hail.
The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees were down in the area from five miles north of Adrian to Meeks in the southern part of the county.
The public observed golf ball-sized hail northeast of Dexter near Harlow.

Numerous reports of hail the size of quarters or larger were received from the public and the Emanuel County Emergency Management Director from across the county.  While most of the hail reported was of the size of quarters, half-dollar to golf ball-sized hail was observed.  In addition, one tree was down on U.S. Highway 221 north.
The public observed quarter-sized hail in the west central part of the county between Norristown, Nunez, and Swainsboro.
Amateur radio operators relayed reports of quarter-sized hail just northwest of Dublin.  Hail was observed on Old Macon Road and Georgia Highway 338 and near the W. H. Bud Baron Airport.
The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported quarter-sized hail from the Meeks area.
The White County Sheriff's Office reported golf ball-sized hail on the southeast side of Cleveland near Truett McConnell College.
The Hall County Sheriff's Office reported that one tree and one power line were down between White Sulfer Road and Georgia Highway 365, approximately two miles northeast of Gainesville.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees were down just south of Ball Ground, one of which had taken out a power line on Ball Ground Highway.  The road had to be closed until the downed power line could be repaired.  Another tree was down just north of Holly Springs.  This tree also took out a power line and blocked a road.

A damage survey conducted by the Cherokee County Emergency Management Director confirmed that a weak EF0 tornado had touched down approximately four miles east-southeast of Holly Springs.  The tornado first touched down on Oak Meadow Drive in a well populated residential neighborhood, then tracked east-northeast approximately 3/4 mile before lifting near the intersection of Waters Road and East Cherokee Drive.  The maximum path width was determined to be 75 yards wide with maximum wind gusts estimated to be 75 mph.  Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted along the path of the tornado.  A number of trees fell on homes resulting in major damage to three homes and minor damage to another 10 homes.  Three outbuildings and three vehicles were destroyed by the fallen trees.

The Oconee County Emergency Management Director reported damage to several trees and power lines in the far southeast part of Oconee County, approximately six to seven miles southeast of Watkinsville.  One vehicle suffered damage from a fallen tree.  The Emergency Management Director was suspicious that the damage appeared to be caused by a tornado as there was a path of damage and trees and power lines were twisted along the path of damage.

The public reported that at least a dozen trees were down on the east and southeast side of Eatonton.  Several power lines were also down.  Some roads were blocked.  Widespread power outages were noted in the area.

The Eatonton Messenger reported that lightning struck a tree in the Oconee National Forest setting the tree on fire.  The fire was contained quickly by the Georgia Forestry Service.  Heavy rain ongoing at the time also helped to keep the fire from spreading.

The Calhoun Times reported that a log cabin, built in the 1840s, on Mountain Loop Road near Sugar Valley in northwest Gordon county suffered extensive damage when a large tree fell through the roof of the structure.  Two other trees were also blown down in the back yard, but these did not cause damage to the home.
The Newnan Times-Herald reported that lightning struck an outbuilding on Providence Church Road just west of Newnan.  The building was apparently destroyed from the resulting fire.

The Newnan Times-Herald wrote that the Coweta County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees and power lines were blown down in the Newnan vicinity.  Trees blocked parts of Fischer Road near Sharpsburg and Belk Road near Newnan.  A couple of power line were also down as a result of downed trees.
The cooperative observer for Rome reported nickel-sized hail in the area three to four miles southeast of Rome.
The Pickens County 911 Center reported that a two to three trees were down in the vicinity of Tate.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that an EF2 tornado touched down near Holland Park Drive in east central Gwinnett county, or about five miles northwest of Dacula.  The tornado then tracked slightly over two miles to the north-northeast between Mountain View High School and Twin Rivers Middle School before lifting just east of the intersection of Gravel Springs Road and Interstate-85.  The tornado was determined to have a path width of 300 yards with maximum wind gusts of 130 mph.  Extensive damage was observed to homes mainly in the Kirkstone Subdivision of Buford.  A total of 56 homes and one business along the path of the tornado sustained at least minor damage.  Of these, 15 to 20 homes sustained major damage or were destroyed and thus were declared uninhabitable.  One of these homes collapsed on itself.  Damage to homes and property was estimated by the state insurance commissioner to exceed $5 million.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that a second, weaker EF0 tornado touched down within the same quasi-linear convective system that spawned the EF2 tornado in Gwinnett county.  This tornado originated in extreme western Butts county approximately four miles southwest of Jenkinsburg, crossed very briefly into extreme eastern Henry county, before crossing back into extreme western Butts county and then lifting immediately thereafter.  The tornado had a total path length of 2.5 miles, mostly in Butts county.  The maximum path width was determined to be 50 yards with maximum wind gusts estimated at 80 mph.  Within Butts county four homes were damaged and at least 200 trees were blown down or uprooted along the path of the tornado.  Several outbuildings were damaged or destroyed, including six storage buildings blown across U.S. Highway 23.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that a second, weaker EF0 tornado touched down within the same quasi-linear convective system that spawned the EF2 tornado in Gwinnett county.  This tornado originated in extreme western Butts county approximately four miles southwest of Jenkinsburg, crossed very briefly into extreme eastern Henry county, before crossing back into extreme western Butts county and then lifting immediately thereafter.  The tornado literally was only 30 feet or so within the Henry county line.  The tornado had a total path length of 2.5 miles, mostly in Butts county.  The maximum path width was determined to be 50 yards with maximum wind gusts estimated at 80 mph.  Damage in Henry county was confined to a gas station/convenience store, which lost part of its awning.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that a second, weaker EF0 tornado touched down within the same quasi-linear convective system that spawned the EF2 tornado in Gwinnett county.  This tornado originated in extreme western Butts county approximately four miles southwest of Jenkinsburg, crossed very briefly into extreme eastern Henry county, before crossing back into extreme western Butts county and then lifting immediately thereafter.  The tornado had a total path length of 2.5 miles, mostly in Butts county.  The maximum path width was determined to be 50 yards with maximum wind gusts estimated at 80 mph.  This final portion of the tornado lasted less than one minute and covered a distance of only 0.1 miles within Butts county.  Damage was confined to a few trees.
The Newton County 911 Center reported that three trees were down along Rocky Plains road in the southern part of the county.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported that a nearby lightning strike damaged his outdoor Christmas holiday lighting.
The Oconee County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the Watkinsville area, one of which was on down on Colham Ferry Road.
The Wilkinson County 911 Center reported that three trees were blown down in the Gordon vicnity.
The Hancock County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees and one power line were down near Lake Sinclair.
The Georgia Forestry commission reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Mill Creek burned 36.5 acres and took four days to contain.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Rockwall burned 1/4 acre causing an esimated $2,500 in damages.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Hall Road burned 46 acres and caused $7,000 in damages.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported that human-caused wildfire labeled Veterans burned 6.5 acres and resulted in $10,000 in damages.
The Georgia Forestry Commission reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Lake burned 1/4 acre and resulted in $1,000 in damages.
The Walker County 911 Center reported snowfall of one inch in the lower elevations to two inches in the higher elevations.
The Dade County 911 Center reported average snowfall of one inch across the county.
The Chattooga County 911 Center reported snowfall of 1/2 inch or less across the county.
The Catoosa County 911 Center reported an average of 1/2 inch of snow across the county.
The Whitfield County 911 Center reported mostly a dusting of snow across the county.
The Gordon County 911 Center reported mostly a dusting of snow across the county.
The Murray County 911 Center reported mostly a dusting of snow across the county.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported generally 1.5 to 2.0 inches of snow across the county.  However, the higher elevations (above 2000 feet) in the northeast part of the county had received up to five inches of snow.

The Pickens County 911 Center reported that snowfall of 1.0 to 1.5 inches was observed across much of the county.  The higher amounts were in the higher elevations across the north part of the county.

The Fannin County 911 Center reported that snowfall ranged from one inch in the lower elevations to two inches in the higher elevations.

The Towns County 911 Center reported that snowfall average about two inches across the county, with isolated near three inch totals in the higher elevations.
The Dade County Emergency Manager reported less than 0.1 inch of glaze ice across the county.  A few accidents were observed on Interstate-59.
The Banks County Emergency Management Director reported less than 0.1 inch of glaze ice across the county.
The Barrow County 911 Center reported less than 0.1 inch of glaze ice across the county.

The Carroll County Emergency Management Director reported up to 0.1 inch of glaze ice across mainly the northern part of the county.  More than 100 traffic accidents were reported in the Villa Rica and Carrollton areas.  One person was injured in a traffic accident on South Carroll Road.
The Bartow County Emergency Management Director reported up to 0.1 inch of glaze ice across the county.  At least 20 traffic accidents were observed, several on Interstate-75.

The Chattooga County Emergency Management Director reported up to 0.1 inch of glaze ice across the county.  Several accidents were reported.  Georgia Highway 27 was closed in the higher elevations between Summerville and the Floyd county line.

The Heard County 911 Center reported about 0.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Henry County 911 Center reported up to 1.0 inch of snowfall across much of the county.
The Jackson County 911 Center reported 2.0 inches of snowfall across most of the county.
The Jasper County 911 Center reported 0.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Jones County 911 Center reported up to 0.5 inch of snowfall across much of the county.
The Lamar County 911 Center reported up to 0.5 inch of snowfall across much of the county.
The Lumpkin County 911 Center reported up to 1.0 inch of snowfall across much of the county.
The Madison County 911 Center reported up to 1.5 inches of snowfall across much of the county.
The Meriwether County 911 Center reported about 0.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Monroe County 911 Center reported up to 0.5 inch of snow across much of the county.
The Morgan County 911 Center reported about 1.5 inches of snowfall across much of the county.
The Murray County 911 Center reported about 0.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Newton County 911 Center reported 1.0 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Oconee County 911 Center reported 1.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Oglethorpe County 911 Center reported that snowfall up to 2.0 inches was observed across much of the county.
The Paulding County 911 Center reported snowfall of 0.5 inch across most of the county.
The Peach County 911 Center reported only a trace of snowfall across most of the county.
The Pickens County 911 Center reported 1.0 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Pike County 911 Center reported generally 0.5 inch of snowfall across the county.
The Polk County 911 Center reported 1.0 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Putnam County 911 Center reported generally 0.5 inch of snowfall across the county.
The Rockdale County 911 Center reported 1.0 inch of snowfall across the county.
The Spalding County 911 Center reported up to 1.0 inch of snowfall across much of the county.
The Talbot County 911 Center reported only a trace of snowfall across most of the county.
The Taliaferro County 911 Center reported 0.5 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Taylor County 911 Center reported that only a trace of snowfall fell across the northern part of the county.
The Towns County 911 Center reported about 1.0 inch of snowfall across most of the county.
The Troup County 911 Center reported about 0.5 inch of snowfall across the county.
The Twiggs County 911 Center reported only a trace of snowfall, mainly in the northern part of the county.
The Union County 911 Center reported snowfall of 1.0 inch across much of the county.
The Upson County 911 Center reported snowfall of 0.5 inch across mainly the northern part of the county.
The Walker County 911 Center reported snowfall of 1.0 inch across most of the county.
The Walton County 911 Center reported up to 2.0 inches of snowfall across the county.
The Warren County 911 Center reported only a trace of snowfall across most of the county.
The White County Emergency Management Director reported snowfall of 1.0 inch across the county.
The Whitfield County 911 Center reported snowfall of 1.5 inches across much of the county.
The Wilkes County 911 Center reported snowfall of 0.5 inch across most of the county.

The Jackson Herald of Jefferson reported that a number of trees were down in the Arcade area.  One home suffered major damage and two others suffered minor damage from trees that fell on the structures.

The Citizen and Georgian of Montezuma reported that the roof over the gas pumps at Wright's Grocery in Oglethorpe was blown off.  Residents in the area claimed that it was a tornado, but there was no supporting evidence of such in the radar data.
The Crisp County 911 Center reported that five trees and one power line were down across the county.  A large sign was also damaged in Cordele.
The Bleckley County 911 Center reported that over a dozen trees were blown down along Georgia Highway 112 southwest of Cary.
The Dodge County 911 Center reported that seven trees and one power line or telephone line were down across the far northern part of the county near Chester.

The Laurens County 911 Center reported that up to a dozen trees and five power lines were down across the western part of the county from Montrose, to Dudley, and Dexter.  Three trees were down on the eastbound side of Interstate-16 near mile marker 42.
The Dodge County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the Milan area.
The Telfair County 911 Center reported that at least nine trees were down across the county, mainly in the McRae area.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that a tree fell on a mobile home in the far western part of the county, approximately eight miles west-northwest of Wrightsville.  The tree punctured the roof of the home.  In addition, four more trees were blown down in the far southern part of the county in the Scott area.

The Treutlen County Emergency Management Director reported that a home in Soperton sustained minor damaged from straight-line thunderstorm winds.  In addition, three trees were blown down near Lothair in the western part of the county.

The Madison County 911 Center reported that a tin roof was blown off a church on Shirley Road just south of the Franklin county line and the city of Royston.  Some two-by-fours were also torn off the same building.  Three trees were down on Shirley Road and Doug Drake Road.  One large pine tree fell on a home causing damage to its roof.  A couple of telephone lines were down along Shirley Road as well.
The Madison County 911 Center reported penny-sized hail in the Shirley Road area just north of Harrison near the Franklin county line.

The Floyd County Emergency Management Director observed flash flooding in Floyd county.  Eighteen roads across the county, mostly in the Rome area, had to be closed from flooding caused by nearby streams, creeks, and drainage ditches.  Water was at least one foot deep in some areas.  In addition, a flag football field was flooded near the Floyd Hospital.  Damage was confined to considerable debris removal.

The Haralson County Emergency Management Director reported that two roads were closed because of flash flooding or small streams and creeks in the area.  Beech Creek Bridge and Francis White Road were closed because of flash flooding when the adjacent creek flowed out of its banks.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal in the area.

The Polk County Emergency Management Director reported that two county roads were flooded caused by nearby streams and drainage ditches.    The roads were just of U.S. Highway 27 near the Haralson county line.  Damage was confined to minor debris removal.

The Gordon County Emergency Management Director reported that several roads were closed because of creek and stream flooding.  Some of the closed roads included Oak Grove Road, Millers Ferry Road, Lanford Road, and Baker Road.  Millers Ferry Road was closed in two locations.  Baker Road had two streams of water flowing over the road.  Damage was confined primarily to minor debris removal.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that several apartments near Battle Creek Parkway in Fort Oglethorpe were flooded with water into the first floors of the buildings.  In addition, twelve roads across the northern part of the county were closed because of flooding.  Damage was confined mostly to debris removal.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia and the Pickens County Emergency Management Director confirmed that extensive damage to trees and property across the northern half of Pickens county was the result of a 75 mph straight-line thunderstorm winds.   Two large chicken houses, just south-southwest of Talking Rock, collapsed and were destroyed.  Eight homes in the same general area suffered minor damage from downed trees and/or tree limbs.  In Jasper, the roof of a large building was removed by the strong winds.  It should be noted, however, that this roof was built on top of an existing roof.  Several power lines were also down in the area between Talking Rock and Jasper.

The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that two homes were struck by lightning in the northern part of the county.  One of the homes was on John Burris Road and the other was along Matt Highway.  No fires were observed, and damage was confined to minor electrical damage.

The Harris County Sheriff's Department, amateur radio operators, and the public observed quarter to golf ball-sized hail across northern Harris county from just east of Whitesville-Pine Lake, to Pine Mountain Valley, to Shiloh.

The public observed quarter-sized hail across the far southern part of Meriwether county.  This was from the same thunderstorm cell that brought golf ball-sized hail to north central and northeast Harris county.
