The Polk County 911 Center reported quarter-sized hail near Cedartown.
The Polk County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down around Cedartown.
The Polk County 911 Center reported golf ball-sized hail near Rockmart.

The Laurens County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down across the northern portion of the county.  WSR-88D base velocity data showed strong winds from near Brewton to Rockledge.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that at least six trees and a couple of power lines were down from two separate areas of thunderstorms that moved across the county in the 1000 to 1030 pm EDT time frame.  The first area affected was just south of Wrightsville, while the second area affected was near Scott.
The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that a well pump house was burned and the fire alarm system at a nursing home were disabled by a lightning strike.
The Jasper County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees and one power line were down in the North Alcovy area in the far northwest part of the county.
The Newton County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the far southern part of the county, near Stewart.
The Telfair County 911 Center reported quarter-sized hail on the northwest side of Workmore.  WSR-88D radar data suggests that similar-sized hail likely continued to just east of Workmore.

The Jefferson County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were down across the northern portion of the county, mainly near Wrens.  The damage was caused by a thunderstorm outflow boundary as an area of thunderstorms moved into the county from the north.

The public reported that many trees and power lines were down across the county.  One tree was down on a vehicle.  Power outages were noted throughout much of the county.  The wind damage was largely caused by an outflow boundary as an area of thunderstorms moved into the county from the north.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported penny to nickel-sized hail northwest of Walnut Grove.  WSR-88D radar data does not support the initial quarter-sized hail reported with this storm.
The public observed golf ball-sized hail just northwest of Soperton.  WSR-88D radar data strongly suggests that hail of similar size likely continued across the county from northwest to southeast.
The Paulding County 911 Center reported golf ball-sized hail near Hiram as yet another round of thunderstorms tracked across the county from west to east.

The Crawford County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were down across the county from strong thunderstorm outflow winds.  Some power lines were also down.  Trees were down on Jackson Road, Tribble Road, Zenith Mill Road, Charlotte Drive, and Knoxville Road.
The Dooly County 911 Center reported that three trees were down within the county.
The Taylor County 911 Center reported that three trees were down within the county.
The Macon County 911 Center reported that three trees were down within the county.

The Peach County 911 Center reported that several trees were down across the county.  The majority of the damage was caused by strong thunderstorm outflow winds well in advance of the actual thunderstorms.
The Pulaski County 911 Center relayed reports of nickel to quarter-sized hail from the eastern part of the county, east of Hawkinsville.

The Montgomery County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees were down on Fire Tower Road, four miles west-northwest of Alston.  The Montgomery County Sheriff's Office reported that one tree was down near Higgston.
The Wheeler County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down across the county, but especially along Georgia Highway 19 just north of Jordan.
The public observed nickel-sized hail near Douglasville.
The Cobb County Emergency Management Director reported that at least a dozen trees were down across the county, but especially in the Mableton area.
The Laurens County 911 Center reported that there were three to four trees and a couple of power lines down south of Dublin.

Several reports of wind damage were received from the Houston County 911 Center.  At least 15 trees were down from just south of Perry to the southern border of the county south of Elko.  A large oak tree was also down in Kathleen.
The Schley County 911 Center reported that three trees were down across the county.
The Houston County Emergency Management Director reported quarter-sized hail near Clinchfield.
The Muscogee County 911 Center reported that one tree and one power line were down on the southeast side of the city of Columbus.
The Troup County 911 Center reported golf ball-sized hail just south of LaGrange and the public observed quarter-sized hail near Smiths Crossroads.
The public observed quarter-sized hail from Cobb to Lake Blackshear in the southeastern part of the county.

An off-duty National Weather Service employee reported that at least 10 trees were down at the Sunset Hills Country Club southwest of Carrollton.  WSB Television of Atlanta reported that a power line was down at a residence northeast of Carrollton.  WSR-88D base velocity data suggested that strong winds, on the order of 50kts or greater, likely translated across the county from northwest of Bowdon to Whitesburg.

The Haralson County 911 Center reported that more than four trees and two power lines were down across the far southern part of the county, generally along and south of a line from Tallapoosa to Bremen.
The Twiggs County 911 Center reported that at least seven trees were down across the northern portion of the county.
The Wilkinson County 911 Center reported that six trees were down in the vicinity of Irwinton and six more trees were down in the vicinity of McIntyre.

The Dade County Emergency Management Director and amateur radio operators reported extensive and widespread wind damage across the northern half of Dade county from an apparent microburst or widespread area of damaging thunderstorm outflow boundary winds.  The most extensive damage was noted in the 9000 block of Scenic Highway, northeast of Trenton.  The most significant damage extended from West Brow to Burkhalter Gap where hundreds of trees were either blown over or uprooted and dozens of power lines were also blown down or affected by downed trees.  Portions of Lookout Mountain Scenic Highway were blocked from dozen of large downed trees.  Two homes in West Brow completely lost their roofs as they were lifted off the structures.  In the 9000 block of Scenic Highway, the roof of one home was blown downstream several hundred feet and wrapped around adjacent trees.  The deck of the home was completely lifted off its foundation and turned on its side.  A nearby chicken farm also sustained damage, including the loss of a number of poultry.  The other home was located in the 8000 block of Scenic Highway and was completely destroyed when its roof was lifted off the structure and thrown across the road.  One of the downed trees on Scenic Highway landed on a vehicle, but no injuries were reported from this incident.  There were also a number of trees down in the northwest part of the county as well.  Several trees were down on Interstate-59, northwest of Trenton.  Widespread power outages were noted across the northern part of the county.
The public reported that more than a dozen trees were down across the northern part of the county, especially just north of Chickamauga in northeast Walker county.  One tree was down on a car.
The public observed penny-sized hail north of Chickamauga.  WSR-88D radar data suggests that similar-size hail likely occurred across much of the northern part of Walker county.

The public reported that at least six trees were down in the county, especially in the Wood Station area in the southern part of the county.  WSR-88D base velocity data suggests that the strong thunderstorm outflow winds that caused extensive damage in Dade and Walker counties likely continued in a diminished fashion into Catoosa county.

Amateur radio operators and the public reported that hundreds of trees were down across the county from west of Rocky Face to Dalton.  Wind gusts were estimated at 65 to 70 mph.  At least 40 homes across the county sustained minor to moderate damage from fallen trees.  Four homes in Dalton and two homes in Rocky Face suffered extensive damage from trees which fell on the structures.  Multiple trees and several power lines were down on Cleveland Highway north of Dalton.  A number of power lines were down throughout the city of Dalton.
The Fannin County 911 Center reported that at least six trees and several power lines were down around Epworth in the western part of the county.
The Gilmer County 911 Center reported that more than a dozen trees were down throughout the county, including the Ellijay area.

The Pickens County Emergency Management Director widespread and extensive tree damage across the county with dozens of trees were down throughout the county.  Several structures were damaged from downed trees and several roads were blocked.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported widespread and extensive damage to trees throughout the county.  No specific damage to structures or vehicles was noted, however.
The Walton County 911 Center relayed a report of golf ball-sized hail from Herndonville and the public observed nickel-sized hail a little further east in Ebenezer.
The Dawson County 911 Center reported that up to 50 trees were down across the county.
The Paulding County 911 Center reported widespread damage to trees across the county.  Dozens of trees were down across the county.

The Atlanta Journal-Contstituation and the Cobb County 911 Center reported that dozens of trees were down throughout the county.  A 55-year old Marietta woman was killed instantly when a large tree fell on her vehicle while traveling along Powers Ferry Road.  Many power outages were noted around the county for up to four hours in some areas.
The public observed quarter-sized hail near and just south of Smyrna.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that several trees and power lines were down across the county.  The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported that several power lines were down in the Buford area.  Several roads were either blocked or at least partially blocked, including East Shadburn Ferry in Buford, South Berkeley Lake Road in Duluth, and Highpoint Road Southwest near U.S. Highway 78 in Snellville.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home in the 2500 block of Cobble Creek Lane in Grayson.  The structure suffered extensive fire, smoke, and water damage.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that multiple structure fires were responded to by fire crews on Zoey Lee Drive Southwest off Temple Johnson Road in Rosebud.  The extent of the damages was not provided.
Severe reports of quarter-sized hail were received from the public from just southwest of Monroe to south and southeast of Monroe, near Herndonville, Ebenezer, and Pannell.
The Walton County 911 Center reported that four trees were down in the vicinity of Monroe.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a good number of trees and power lines were down throughout Fulton county.  Some roads were blocked from downed trees and power lines.  A woman had to be rescued from her vehicle when a tree fell on it at the intersection of Grandview and Pharr Road in Buckhead.  Several other vehicles were also damaged during this accident.  The woman was not injured.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that several trees and power lines were down throughout the county.
The Barrow County 911 Center reported that at least 11 trees were down in the vicinity of County Line in the northwest and north central part of the county.

The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down.  Up to four homes sustained minor to moderate damage from downed trees.  Several power lines were down.  Some roads were temporarily blocked from downed trees and power lines.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that a number of trees and power lines were down throughout Hall county.  The Hall County Emergency Management Director reported damage to a traffic signal and billboard in the far southern part of the county near the Gwinnett county line, just east of Rest Haven.  In addition, there was damage at the Road Atlanta Lanier Speedway in the far southeast portion of the county.  Several canopies were blown over and damaged some of the race cars being used during a Saturday evening racing event.  A flag in the infield was ripped from the top of the pole.  Several trees and large tree limbs were also down in the woods surrounding the track and strewn about the grounds of the facility.
The Oconee County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were down from Watkinsville to east of Bishop.
The Oglethorpe County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were down in the county, mainly in the Lexington and Crawford areas.

The Clarke County Emergency Management Director reported that at least four trees and over six power lines were down in the Athens area.  Much of the city of Athens was left without power for several hours following the damaging thunderstorm winds.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that lightning ignited a fire at a residence in Athens located on Ashbrook Drive.  Specific details regarding damages were not provided.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported penny-sized hail near Jones Mill and Colwell.

The public reported that there was considerable wind damage within the city of Commerce in the northeast part of the county.  Several trees were blown down across the city.  A large billboard sign was blown down as the pole was snapped in half and splintered.
A meteorologist with Georgia Public Television reported penny-sized hail in north Fulton county near Roswell.
The public and the Murray County 911 Center reported that dozens of trees and power lines were down across the county.
The public observed half-dollar-sized hail near Ramhurst.
The public observed penny-sized hail.
The Walker County 911 Center reported that over a dozen trees were down in the Lookout Mountain area in the northwestern and northern part of the county.
The Chattooga County Emergency Management Director reported that at least six trees were down across the county.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that over a dozen trees were down in the Fort Oglethorpe area, with at least five trees down on power lines in other areas across the northern part of the county.
The Wilkinson County Emergency Management Director reported that at least 10 trees were down in the Irwinton area.

The Douglas County Emergency Management Director reported that strong thunderstorm winds blew a number of shingles off the Douglas County High School.  In addition, three trees were blown down on North Burnt Hickory Road and another tree was down at the intersection of Post and Poole Roads.

The DeKalb County 911 Center reported that at least two large trees and more than six power lines were down across the county.  At least one home on Dahlia Drive, three miles east-southeast of Decatur, sustained damage from a fallen tree.  Power lines were down on McClendon Drive and a tree was down on U.S. Highway 78 near Mountain Industrial Boulevard.  A trained spotter recorded a wind gust of 60 mph at 415 pm EDT near Gresham Park.

The Fulton County Emergency Management Director reported that power lines were down across many areas of the county.  The worst damage was in the area approximately six miles south-southeast of Atlanta near Hapeville, Lakewood Park, and Grant Park.

The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported that at least six trees and five power lines were down, especially in the western half of the county.  WSR-88D base velocity data suggests that strong winds likely continued across the entire county as a strong gust front associated with a line of thunderstorms.
The Walton County Emergency Management Director reported that a few trees and power lines were down across mainly the northern half of the county, especially in the Campton area.

The Barrow County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down across the county.  The most concentrated damage was noted between Auburn, Carl, and Winder in the northwest part of the county.
The Jackson County 911 Center reported that two trees were down on two different power lines in the northeast part of the county near Apple Valley and Commerce.
The Madison County 911 Center reported that a tree was down on a power line in Colbert.

The Oconee County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down throughout the county.  Among other locations, trees were down on Moores Mill, Ridgeway and power lines were down on Malcolm Bridge, and Lenru Roads.

The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that a large tree was down on a home four miles west of Woodstock, causing damage to the structure.  A power line was down three miles north of Canton, and two to three trees were down in the southeast part of the county, near Hickory Flat.  The emergency manager measured the wind gusts at 41 mph in Canton.

The Lumpkin County Emergency Management Director relayed reports of a brief period of quarter-sized hail just northwest of Dahlonega, with mostly nickel-sized hail on the north and northeast side of Dahlonega.  The public observed nickel-sized hail between Dahlonega and Garland in the southeast part of the county.  There was also one tree down on Longbranch Road at GA 115W.
The Catoosa County 911 Center reported that about six trees and power lines were down in the northwest part of the county near Fort Oglethorpe.
The public observed nickle-sized hail near Ringgold.
The Dade County 911 Center reported that up to five trees were down in the Poplar Springs Road area.
The Walker County 911 Center reported that up to five trees and one power line were down just north of Chickamauga in northern Walker county.
The Whitfield County Emergency Management Director reported that a commercial structure on Beaverdale Road was set on fire by lightning.  No specific details regarding damages were provided.
The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that up to seven trees were down in the northeast part of the county near Cherry Log.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that four trees were blown down from another round of thunderstorms.  The first thunderstorm was an isolated cell that only affected the northeast part of the county.  The second area of thunderstorm activity was a line that moved across the entire county from northwest to southeast.
The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported that penny-sized hail fell across the northeast part of the county between Cherry Log and Pisgah.
The Floyd County 911 Center reported that at least nine trees were down across the county, mainly just southwest of Rome.
The Floyd County Emergency Management Director observed penny-sized hail just south of Lindale near Silver Creek.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that three trees were down in the far southwestern portion of the county.
The Coweta County 911 Center reported that a power pole was struck and taken out by a lightning strike.
The Carroll County 911 Center reported that at least 10 trees were down across the county.

The public observed quarter-sized hail on Jacksonville Road north of Tallapoosa and west of Buchanan.  WSR-88D radar data suggests that similar-sized hail likely continued to the northeast and toward Buchanan.
The Douglas County Emergency Management Director reported that a tree was blown down onto a home on Cherokee Drive in Douglasville.
The Emergency Manager for the Georgia Institute of Technology observed penny-sized hail on the Georgia Tech Campus.
The Coweta County 911 Center reported that at least 11 trees were down across the county.
The Douglas County 911 Center reported that a tree fell on a vehicle on Bomar Road in Chapel Hill.
The Coweta County 911 Center reported that a home in Sharpsburg was struck by lightning.  No fire ensued and damages were minor.
The public observed penny-sized hail on the east side of Athens.
The Cobb County Emergency Management Director reported penny-sized hail near Acworth.
An amateur radio operator relayed a report of intermittent penny-sized hail from the Thomas Crossroads area.
The public observed half-dollar-sized hail just southwest and south of Cooper Heights.

Several reports of penny to nickel-sized hail were received from the public across northwest and north central Hall county, near Murrayville and Clermont.
The Hall County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a tree causing the tree to fall on the adjacent home resulting in damage to the structure.

The public measured a wind gust of 69 mph in Lyerly at 505pm EDT.  Two trees were reported down by the Chattooga County 911 Emergency Management Director.  One tree was down on Georgia Highway 114 and another was down on Spring Creek Road.

The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that at least half-a-dozen trees and four power lines were down from Armuchee to Rome, Lindale, and Silver Creek. A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia and the Cherokee County Emergency Manager confirmed that an EF1 tornado, spawned by strong shear associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Lee, touched down in southern Cherokee county, just south of the Dixie Speedway, or just west of Woodstock, then tracked north-northeast across eastern Cherokee county before moving into southeastern Pickens county near the city of Nelson.  The tornado, with a semi-continuous path nearly 24 miles long across Cherokee county, had a maximum path width of 1/4 mile and maximum wind gusts of 90 mph.  The tornado caused extensive damage to homes and business across eastern Cherokee county.  The Brookshire and Town Lake Hills South subdivisions sustained much of the structural damage within the county.  The Dixie Speedway, just west of Woodstock, suffered extensive damage as well.  A number of recreational vehicles and boats were parked at the facility in anticipation of an event.  Dozens of these were overturned and destroyed by the tornado.  Over 600 single-family homes sustained some form of structural damage, with seven of these homes completely destroyed.  One injury was confirmed at one of the heavily damaged homes.  A total of 148 homes sustained major damage and 269 sustained minor damage.  In addition, six apartment units sustained damage, with three of these classified as having major damage.  Twenty commercial businesses were affected by the tornado, three of which were destroyed.  Sixteen of these businesses suffered major damage.  Finally, three churches sustained damage, two of which suffered major damage.  In addition to the structural damage, hundreds of trees were damaged or destroyed by the tornado, many of which subsequently caused damage to adjacent structures and dozens of vehicles.||[09/05/11: Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF1, Cherokee-Pickens, 2011:025].

The remnants of Tropical Storm Lee impacts north and central Georgia with one EF1 tornado and modest to heavy rainfall across the northwest half of the state.  Rainfall ranged from near eight inches in parts of northwest Georgia to less than one inch in the southeast part of the county warning area.  An EF1 tornado caused extensive damage in Cherokee county during the afternoon of September 5th.  The annual Atlanta Motor Speedway event on Sunday September 4th was rained out and had to be postponed to a later date.  Winds associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Lee were generally less than 20 mph by the time it reached the region.

The Pickens County Emergency Management Director confirmed that the EF1 tornado, which originally touched down in far southern Cherokee county just west of Woodstock and continued on a north-northeastward track across eastern Cherokee county, entered Pickens county at the city of Nelson.  Damage in Pickens county remained consistent with an EF1 rating.  From here, the tornado continued north-northeast to just past Marble Hill before finally lifting.  Within Pickens county the tornado had a path length of approximately five miles with a maximum path width of 220 yards or 1/8 mile.  Eleven homes were damaged along the path of the tornado within Pickens county.  One of these homes was completely removed from its foundation and destroyed.  Four other homes suffered major damage, three with moderate damage, and the remaining three minor damage.  The majority of this damage was in the Marble Hill community.  In addition, three structures at the Emory Marble Plant in Marble Hill suffered major damage.  Dozens of medium to large-sized trees, including several large oak trees, were downed along the path of the tornado. The Paulding County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down in the Hiram vicinity. A storm spotter observed three to five trees down near Georgia Highway 52 southeast of Cartecay close to the Dawson county line.

The public observed a funnel cloud near Buckhead in eastern Morgan county.  WSR-88D storm-relative velocity data detected two strong rotation areas moving across Morgan county at the time, one which had just moved into Oconee county and another moving up from the southwest between Madison and Buckhead.  A tornado warning was in effect for Morgan county at the time.
The public observed a funnel cloud near Arnoldsville.  WSR-88D storm-relative velocity data showed strong rotation in the area at the time.  A tornado warning was in effect for this area at the time.
The Bartow County 911 Center reported that over a dozen trees were down from just south to just west of Cassville in central Bartow county.

The Dade County Emergency Management Director reported that several small creeks in the county were overflowing their banks causing portions of adjacent roads to become flooded.  One home near Georgia Highway 136 in Trenton became surrounded by flood waters from Sitton Gulch Creek.  The residents of this home had to be evacuated by the Trenton Fire Department.  Monetary damage was a result of minor damage to the affected home and debris removal.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that the Black Branch Creek flooded the parking lot of the Battlewood Apartments in Fort Oglethorpe.  Several evacuations were required at the apartment complex as the water level reached the steps of several of the units.  Several other small creeks in the county also overflowed their banks.  Despite the evacuations, none of the apartment units were actually flooded or incurred any damages.  Monetary damage was confined to debris removal.

The Walker County Emergency Management Director reported that several creeks across the northern half of the county were overflowing their banks and flooding the normally flood prone areas of adjacent roadways.  Monetary damage was confined to minor debris removal.
The Muscogee County 911 Center reported that more than half-a-dozen trees and power lines were down across the county, especially in the Columbus area.
The Jones County 911 Center reported that two to three trees and two to three power lines were down in south central and central part of the county from near Postell to just north of James.

The Jones County 911 Center reported that two to three trees and two to three power lines were down.  WSR-88D velocity and storm-relative velocity data suggested that this occured in the west central and northwest part of the county near Jarrell Plantation and southwest of Round Oak.

The Chattooga County Emergency Management Director reported that strong winds associated with the core remnants of Tropical Storm Lee combined with the wet ground brought down dozens of trees across the county.

The Whitfield County Emergency Management Director reported that nearly two dozen trees and several power lines were down across the county as a result of strong winds associated with the core remnants of Tropical Storm Lee.

The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees and power lines were down in the Texas Valley area located in the northern part of the county.  The strong winds were associated with the core remnants of Tropical Storm Lee as it passed just northwest of the region.

The Catoosa County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees were down in the northern part of the county near Ringgold, especially on Crest Drive and Thompson Hill Road just west of Ringgold. The Greene County 911 Center relayed a report from a Georgia Department of Natural Resources Agent of a funnel cloud on Georgia Highway 15 near Ward Road. The Whitfield County Emergency Management Director reported that a tree was blown over onto a home during a thunderstorm associated with Tropical Storm Lee.  The home sustained moderate structural damage as a result.

The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported flash flooding in the Tinsley Mill Village area of Peachtree City. The Coweta County Emergency Management Director reported that a second home was struck by lightning.  This home was located at 220 Spring Forest Way, again in the Thomas Crossroads area.  No fire occurred and only minor electrical damage was observed.

The Coweta County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck yet a third home, this time in western Coweta county.  The home suffered extensive fire and smoke damage as a result of the lightning strike, rendering the home uninhabitable.

The remnants of Tropical Storm Lee impacts north and central Georgia with one EF1 tornado and modest to heavy rainfall across the northwest half of the state.  Rainfall ranged from near eight inches in parts of northwest Georgia to less than one inch in the southeast part of the county warning area.  An EF1 tornado caused extensive damage in Cherokee county during the afternoon of September 5th.  The annual Atlanta Motor Speedway event on Sunday September 4th was rained out and had to be postponed to a later date.  Winds associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Lee were generally less than 20 mph by the time it reached the region.
Several reports of nickel to quarter-sized hail were received from the public from Macon, east-southeastward toward Dry Branch, including much of the east central part of the county.
The public observed quarter-sized hail in the Dry Branch area near the Bibb county line.

Amateur radio operators reported a thunderstorm downburst just southeast of Macon that caused considerable damage to trees and property in the area.  At least 14 trees were either uprooted or blown over.  The downed trees caused minor to moderate damage to three structures in the area.

The Twiggs County 911 Center reported that three trees were down near Bullard.  WSR-88D velocity data suggests that strong winds from a thunderstorm downburst in Bibb county likely also affected the Dry Branch area, as there was damage on the Bibb county side of the line.
The Twiggs County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a tree near Jeffersonville, setting the tree on fire.
The Hancock County Emergency Management Director relayed a report of quarter-sized hail from just east-northeast of Beulah in the far south central part of the county.
The Butts County 911 Center reported half-dollar-sized hail just northeast of Jackson.
The Jackson County 911 Center relayed a report of penny-sized hail in the Turtle Cove area near the Butts county line.
The public observed golf ball-sized hail just south of Wadley in the far southern part of the county.

FOX 5 Television of Atlanta relayed a report of strong thunderstorm downburst winds that caused damage in the Lake Jackson area in the far eastern part of Butts county along the Jasper county line.  Several large trees and power lines were down with at least one tree on the home with roof damage.

The Harris County 911 Center reported that over a dozen trees and several power lines were down across the southern one-half of the county, roughly from Mountain Hill to just Waverly Hall and southward.  Two homes sustained minor to moderate damage from downed trees.  Trees were down along Georgia Highways 219 and 103 south of Hamilton.  Several other local or county roads were blocked by downed trees.
The Crisp County Emergency Management Director reported that a number of trees were down across the southern part of the county near the Turner County line from west to east of Arabi.

The public observed quarter-sized hail at the Plantation House, approximately four miles east-northeast of Arabi.  The Crisp County Emergency Management Director reported penny-sized hail approximately four miles northwest of Arabi, near the intersection of U.S. Highway 41 and Georgia Highway 33.
An amatuer radio operator measured a wind gust of 60 mph on a home weather station just west-northwest of McRae.
An amateur radio operator observed quarter-sized hail just west-northwest of McRae.
The public observed quarter-sized hail at the Dollar General Store in Uvalda.
The Glascock County Emergency Management Director reported that up to 15 large trees were down across the county, including one which fell on and took out a power line.
The Wilcox County Emergency Management Director reported that up to eight trees were down near Rochelle, with a couple causing minor damage to homes.
The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director relayed a report of penny-sized hail from the far southern part of the county, southwest of Woodstock.

The Cobb County 911 Center reported that several trees, at least six, were down across the east central part of the county near Smyrna and Marietta.  Power outages were also noted in the Powder Springs area in the southwest part of the county.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that an EF2 tornado caused extensive damage across Harris county.  The tornado first touched down as an EF1 in Macon county, Alabama before moving east into Lee county, Alabama and then into Harris county, Georgia.  The tornado had already caused considerable damage to the town of Auburn, Alabama as an EF1 before it continued into Harris county, Georgia.  As the tornado approached the county seat of Hamilton, it strengthened to an EF2. The tornado entered Harris county from Alabama at the north end of Lake Harding and tracked across the central part of the county, then moved into extreme northwest Talbot county before lifting, approximately two miles east-northeast of the town of Shiloh on the Harris/Talbot county line.  The tornado had already carved out a path over 33 miles in length across eastern Alabama before it moved into Georgia.  Within Harris county, the tornado path length was approximately 26 miles.  The maximum path width was determined to be 1/2 mile with maximum winds of 125 mph.  The tornado caused considerable damage across Harris county, especially around the county seat of Hamilton.  Two homes were completely destroyed, with 68 other structures suffering minor to moderate damage, including 22 county buildings.  County buildings damaged included the Harris County School Complex, the Harris County 911 Center, the Harris County Animal Shelter, and the agricultural center.  One of the structures heavily damaged was a mobile home, where a man and his wife sustained minor injuries.  Hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted along the path of the tornado.||[11/16/11:  Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF2, Harris-Talbot, 2011:026].
The Murray County 911 Center reported that 15 to 20 trees were down across the northern part of Chatsworth, mostly near Old Federal Road North.  No structural damage was reported.

The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that a tree fell on a sport utility vehicle (SUV) killing a 51-year old male inside the vehicle.  The incident took place on Brookwood Drive near McGinnis Ferry Road in the Johns Creek portion of far southern Forsyth county.  The person inside the vehicle was killed instantly.  One other tree was down in the northern part of the county as well.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that the EF1 to EF2 tornado, that first touched down in Macon county Alabama and tracked across all of Harris county, continued into extreme northwest Talbot county before lifting.  The tornado tracked on the ground over 33 miles within Alabama, 26 miles within Harris county, and approximately two miles within Talbot county for a total path length of nearly 61 miles.  The tornado decreased to an EF1 before it entered Talbot county and the path width decreased to less than 1/2 mile.  Damage within Talbot county was confined to several downed trees and power lines in the far northwest part of the county along Old Shiloh Road.||[11/16/11:  Tornado #1, County #2-2, EF2, Harris-Talbot, 2011:026].
The Monroe County 911 Center reported that a few trees were down in the west central part of the county between the county line just east of Johnstonville and the city of Forsyth.

The Twiggs County 911 Center reported that at least six trees were down in the northwest part of the county near Huber.  Several of the trees were down on Interstate-16 and two trees were down on U.S. Highway 129.  Power outages were observed in the area.
The Wilkinson County 911 Center reported that approximately five trees were down from the Twiggs county line west of McIntyre into the McIntyre and Irwinton areas.
The public observed nickel to quarter-sized hail across the central part of the county near Sandersville.
The Jefferson County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees and power lines were down in the far northern part of the county, generally between Stapleton and Wrens.

The Laurens County 911 Center reported that several trees were down across the far northern part of the county.  Amateur radio operators reported that the roof was torn off a barn and a grain elevator was flipped over between Dublin and the Wilkinson/Johnson county line as well.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that thunderstorm winds had caused significant damage across Johnson county.  A total of six homes sustained damage, mostly minor to moderate.  However, one home suffered significant damage when a large pine tree fell through the structure.  An adjacent car was also heavily damaged.  A portion of a carport was also blown up on the roof of the home.  Several pump houses being built were blown several feet away from their original location.  A total of 16 large trees were down across the county.

The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported hail the size of quarters, possibly a little larger, in the Wrightsville area.  The hail continued from west to east across mainly the northern sections of the county.

Amateur radio operators reported that several trees were down across the far northern part of the county near the Jefferson county line.  Portions of McGarrs Mill Pond Road were blocked from downed trees.
Amateur radio operators relayed a report of quarter-sized hail from the far northern part of the county, just south of the Jefferson county line.
The Toombs County 911 Center reported that three trees were down near Lyons, one of which was down on a power line.
The Washington County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were down throughout the county.
An amateur radio operator observed quarter-sized hail near the Houston county courthouse.

The Houston County Emergency Management Director reported that an apparent microburst along the leading edge of a line of thunderstorms completely destroyed a chicken house.  The damage was extremely localized as none of the neighboring structures suffered any damage.

The United States Forecast Service confirmed that a wildfire, labeled Martin Mill, affected a 5.3 acre area of Putnam county.  The cause of the fire was indicated to be lightning, although no thunderstorm activity was observed in the area at the time.  Damages related to the fire were estimated at $1,500.

An employee of the Dawson County Emergency Management Agency reported that up to two inches of snow was observed in the Burnt Mountain area of northwest Dawson county, straddling the Pickens county line.  Snow accumulation was mostly confined to grassy surfaces because of warm ground temperatures.  This image was taken at the fire station on Burnt Mountain in far northwest Dawson county.

An employee of the Dawson County Emergency Management Agency reported that up to two inches of snow was observed in the Burnt Mountain area of northeast Pickens county, straddling the Dawson county line.  Snow accumulation was mostly confined to grassy surfaces because of warm ground temperatures.
The Polk County 911 Center reported that two to three trees were down along U.S. Highway 278 near Esom Hill.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia, confirmed that an EF2 tornado, the first of six tornadoes to affect west Georgia on this day, touched down approximately three miles west-southwest of Rome, then continued on a northeastward track approximately 12 miles before lifting about 7 1/4 miles north-northeast of Rome.  The tornado was determined to have a maximum path width of 200 yards with maximum winds estimated to be 125 mph.  As the tornado first touched down just west of Rome, it was classified as an EF1 but strengthened to an EF2 as it moved toward the community of Walton Creek.  The tornado remained at an EF2 intensity for approximately 1 1/2 miles as it crossed Georgia Highway 20.  The tornado eventually lifted and dissipated just west of Georgia Highway 53, just north of Jones Bend Road.  At least 20 homes along the path of the tornado sustained significant damage.  Many trees and several power lines were also damage or destroyed by the tornado.  In addition, three minor injuries were reported at one of the damaged homes.  Numerous trees and power lines were down along the path of the tornado as well, including along Georgia Highway 27, Division Street, Shorter Avenue, Edmond Road, and Elm Street.  Some traffic signals were also blown down.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF2, Floyd, 2011:027].

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City confirmed a second tornado touchdown in extreme northeast Floyd county, northeast of Pinson, just north of Georgia Highway 140.  Within Floyd county the tornado remained at an EF0 intensity with a path width of 440 yards or 1/4 mile.  The tornado quickly moved into extreme northwest Bartow county, and then into Gordon county where it eventually intensified to an EF3 causing considerable damage.  This tornado was also determined to have begun from the same circulation that was earlier responsible for an EF2 tornado just west to just north of Rome, which caused significant damage to at least 20 homes in that area.  Damage with this EF0 tornado in extreme northeast Floyd county was confined to several trees.  No structural damage was observed.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #2, County #1-3, EF3, Floyd-Bartow-Gordon, 2011:028].

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that the EF0 tornado that touched down in extreme northeast Floyd county continued into extreme northwest Bartow county before continuing into Gordon county.  The tornado remained at EF0 intensity across extreme northwest Gordon county with a maximum path width of 440 yards.  Damage survey members observed and county emergency personnel reported that a number of trees were down along Oak Grove Road just north of Georgia Highway 140.  A few homes in this area also sustained minor to moderate damage from downed trees.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #2, County #2-3, EF3, Floyd-Bartow-Gordon, 2011:028].

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that the EF0 tornado, that initially touched down in extreme northeast Floyd county and continued across extreme northwest Bartow county, continued into Gordon county.  The tornado entered Gordon county about 2.8 miles east-southeast of Plainville before continuing on a northeastward track into central Gordon county, lifting and dissipating on the east side of Calhoun.  The tornado strengthened to an EF1 almost immediately after entering Gordon county, then to an EF3 as it approached the south side of Calhoun.  At its maximum intensity and size the tornado was determined to be 880 yards or 1/2 mile wide and had maximum winds of 150 mph.  The tornado tracked at least 10 miles through Gordon county.  As the tornado entered Gordon county, several homes along Emily Lane were damaged from falling trees just east of Plainville.  As the tornado strengthened to an EF3 near the corner of Boone Ford Road and Beason Road just south of Calhoun, were several additional homes were damaged and one was completely destroyed.  Numerous trees and power lines were also down along the path of the tornado through Gordon county, including several blocking Interstate-75 near the Bartow county line.  Four injuries were also reported from the destroyed home.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #2, County #3-3, EF3, Floyd-Bartow-Gordon, 2011:028].

The Coweta County 911 Center reported that several power lines were down on Mount Carmel Road between Arnco-Sargent and Plant Yates.  WSR-88D radar data suggests that strong winds or perhaps a mesoscale circulation impacted this area and northeast toward Dunaway Gardens and Roscoe.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that a brief EF1 tornado affected south central Coweta county.  While damage was initially determined to be caused by strong straight line winds responsible for isolated tree and power line damage just north of Grantville, a brief EF1 tornado subsequently touched down as the storm progressed further northeast.  The tornado touched down approximately two miles southwest of Moreland and tracked on the ground for just slightly over one mile, lifting approximately 1.2 miles southwest of Moreland.  The tornado was determined to have a maximum path width of 100 yards with maximum winds of 90 mph.  EF1 tornado damage began immediately upon touchdown along Polk Road where dozens of trees were snapped.  Tree damage continued to the northeast along Dingler Road.  One home on Polk Road sustained substantial damage to its roof.  Several trees were also uprooted or snapped on this property as well.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #4, County #1-1, EF1, Coweta, 2011:030].
The Douglas County 911 Center reported that three trees were down in the Winston area.

The Gilmer County Emergency Management Director reported and the Cherokee County Emergency Management Director discovered an area of damage in southwest Gilmer county.  The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director determined that the damage was the result of an EF1 tornado.  The tornado touched down approximately four miles southeast of Carters (in Murray county) in far southwest Gilmer county near Georgia Highway 136.  The tornado tracked on the ground, paralleling Georgia Highway 136, in an east-northeastward direction for only 1.5 miles before lifting near the intersection of Camp Branch Road and Georgia Highway 136.  The damage path was determined to be 300 yards wide with maximum winds estimated to be 90 mph.  The most significant damage resulting from the tornado was to the Shady Grove Church, which sustained minor damage from falling trees.  No other structures were damaged.  However, a total of at least 100 trees and six power poles were snapped or downed by the tornado.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #3, County #1-1, EF1, Gilmer, 2011:029].

The Troup County 911 Center reported that several trees were down in the Hogansville area.  WSR-88D radar indicates that a developing mesoscale circulation was evident in this area, which subsequently moved rapidly northeast and spawned a brief EF1 tornado in south central Coweta county, just southwest of Moreland.

The Meriwether County 911 Center reported that a few trees were down in the Primrose Community.  WSR-88D indicated a mesoscale circulation developing in the area at the time, which later tracked across far south and southeast Fayette county spawning a brief EF1 tornado near Lake Horton.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City, Georgia confirmed that a brief and weak EF1 tornado touched down in far southeast Fayette county along the northeast shore of Lake Horton.  The tornado first touched down near the end of Woolsey Creek Trail just west of Georgia Highway 92.  The tornado then moved northeast a total of 1.6 miles, lifting just north of the end of Mudbridge Road and just shy of the Clayton county line.  Intermittent tree damage was observed along the path of the tornado with a total of 35 trees snapped or downed.  Two homes sustained minor roof damage and two outbuildings, including a large barn, were destroyed.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #5, County #1-1, EF1, Fayette, 2011:031].

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Peachtree City confirmed that a brief EF0 tornado affected far north Fayette county.  The tornado touched down near Lees Mill Road just west of Georgia Highway 92 and traveled northeast about one mile before lifting just northeast of the end of Hill Road.  Approximately 50 trees and six power poles were downed or snapped along the path of the tornado, especially along Hill Road.  One home on Hill Road lost several shingles, a few gutters, and a portion of the flashing on its roof.  A wooden fence was also destroyed at the same property from downed trees.  WSR-88D also indicated that the circulation that spawned this tornado was likely associated with the same circulation that earlier spawned an EF1 tornado in Coweta county.||[12/22/11:  Tornado #6, County #1-1, EF0, Fayette, 2011:032].
The Harris County Emergency Management Director reported that two trees were down in the Lake Harding Backwater area and two more trees were down on O Street, just northeast of downtown Hamilton.

The Clayton County 911 Center reported that one tree was down at the intersection of Panhandle Road and Woolsey Road near the Fayette county line, a couple of trees were down at the intersection of Tara Boulevard and Old Town Place, and a couple of trees were down at the intersection of Lake Jodeco Road and Camp Road, all in the Jonesboro area.
The Henry County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were down around Hampton and a couple more trees were down in the McDonough area.

The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that several trees and power lines were down across the county.  A tree was blown down onto a home just southwest of Cumming causing minor damage to the structure.
The public reported that a couple of trees were down on power lines within the city of Monroe at the intersection of Youth Monroe Road and Georgia Highway 81.
A United States Forest Service Employee reported 0.75 inch hail in the Villanow area.
A member of the general public reported 0.88 inch hail on Corporate Drive in Dalton.
A trained storm spotter reported 0.75 inch hail near Chatsworth.
A member of the general public reported 0.75 inch hail just south of Williamson.
The Catoosa County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down across the county.
The Floyd County Emergency Manager reported that three trees were blown down across the county.  One fell on a house in the Silvercreek community.
The Fannin County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down county wide.
The Gilmer County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down county wide.
The Cherokee County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down county wide.
The Dawson County 911 Center reported that many trees and several power lines were blown down county wide.
The Lumpkin County 911 Center reported that  many trees were blown down county wide.
The Hall County 911 Center reported that many trees were blown down county wide.  Some trees fell on homes.
The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported one tree down in Snellville.
The Forsyth County 911 Center reported that many trees and several powerlines were blown down across the county.
The Towns County 911 Center reported that four trees were blown down across the county.
The White County 911 Center reported that three trees were blown down across the county.
Amateur radio operators reported 1.00 inch hail from Concord to Meansville.
The Lamar County 911 Center reported hail between 1.00 and 1.75 inches across Barnesville.
Georgia Power reported 1.00 inch hail in Juliette.
A member of the general public reported 1.00 inch hail south of Eastman.
A member of the general public reported 1.00 inch hail south of Uvalda.
The public reported 0.88 inch hail southwest of Winston.
The broadcast media reported 1.75 inch hail southwest of Atlanta.
Broadcast media and the Muscogee County 911 Center reported numerous reports of large hail across the northern part of the county, ranging in size from 1.00 to 1.75 inches.
The public reported 1.00 inch hail just west of McRae.
The Dooly County Emergency Manager reported 0.88 inch hail in Unadilla.

The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported that signs at a shopping plaza were blown out and others twisted at the intersection of Fairburn Road and Shawnee Trail.  Several businesses along Fairburn Road sustained minor structural damage to the roofs, with another sustaining moderate damage.  One window was blown out, and several tree limbs were downed.
The Heard County 911 Center reported that numerous trees were blown down along Highway 34 East in Franklin.

Senoia Police and the Coweta County Emergency Manager reported that one tree was blown down near Howard Road and another at the entrance to the Willow Dale Subdivision.  Minor wind damage occurred at a recreational baseball field, including a score board and dugout shelters.  There was also minor damage sustained to the porch of the nearby senior center.
The Meriwether County 911 Center reported that two trees were blown down.
The Lamar County 911 Center reported that three trees and a power line were down on a transformer in Barnesville.
The Harris County 911 Center reported that 10 to 12 trees were blown down along Highways 219 and 116 near Interstate 185.
The Columbus media relayed a report of numerous trees across River Road in northern Muscogee County.
The Cobb County 911 Center reported that two trees were blown down near Tibor Drive and Pitner Road.
The Monroe County Emergency Manager reported that 0.88 inch hail was coming down in sheets and had accumulated to a depth of a quarter of an inch in the city of Forsyth.

The water level at three USGS stream gauges exceeded flood stage. Snapfinger Creek at Redan Road and South Fork Peachtree Creek at Johnson Road exceeded 12 feet, and Intrenchment Creek at Constitution Road exceeded 11 feet. Minor flooding occurred in some backyards, parks and the natural flood plain near these creeks.

Around 7 roads had minor flooding due to tributaries and streams in the upper South River and Intrenchment Creek basins overflowing.  There were at least 6 inches of water temporarily blocking the roads.

The water level at a USGS stream gauge exceeded flood stage of 12 feet on the Lookout Creek at Creek Road.  Minor flooding also occurred along the creek at Sells Lane in Trenton and Mason Road near Rising Fawn.

A branch flowing into Fausett Creek washed out a portion of Raven Cliff Road. Debris blockage at the culvert pipe and the volume of water caused the branch to overflow the rock based road and cause significant erosion.

The water level at a USGS stream gauge exceeded flood stage of 12 feet on the Lookout Creek at Creek Road.  Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields along the creek. The water overflowed portions of Sells Lane in Trenton and Mason Road near Rising Fawn and caused minor flooding.

A National Weather Service assessment team determined than an EF-0 tornado occurred in north Dooly County.  The weak EF-0 tornado initially touched down around 415 PM with winds around 80 MPH along Old National Road northwest of Pinehurst where several trees were downed.  The weak tornado lifted and briefly touched down again along Highway 41 near Taylor Road where several trees were uprooted.  Near Rocky Ford Road, three outbuildings were damaged or destroyed.  Sheets of tin were torn off a barn, the roof was blown off a hay shelter, and another hay shelter collapsed.  The damage path was sporadic as the weak tornado would quickly lift after only brief touchdowns along the path. The final tree damage noted was along 3rd District Road just north of Highway 27 where several trees were downed.||[01/21/12: Tornado #3, County #1-1, EF0, Dooly, 2012:003].

A National Weather Service assessment team determined that an EF-1 tornado occurred in southeast Macon County.  The tornado initially touched down as EF-0 with winds around 75 MPH along Highway 128 just north of Oglethorpe.  The tornado then strengthened to an EF-1 with maximum winds near 110 MPH along Highway 49 near Four Points where a house was destroyed and numerous trees were snapped and uprooted.  The tornado continued east-southeast, causing significant damage along Mennonite School Road just north of Highway 26 where two large chicken houses were completely destroyed and another was significantly damaged.  The tornado lifted as an EF-0 near Five Points along Highway 26.  Overall, an estimated 25 trees were downed or snapped, approximately five houses received roof damage, one house lost its porch and another house was completely destroyed.  Three large chicken houses were damaged or destroyed and one barn roof was lifted off.||[01/21/12: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Macon, 2012:002].

A National Weather Service assessment team determined that an EF-1 tornado occurred in south central Coweta County.  The tornado initially touched down around 12:10 PM as an EF-0 with winds around 75 MPH near the intersection of Alex Stephens and Gordon Roads just northeast of Moreland.  The tornado then strengthened quickly to an EF-1 with maximum winds near 110 MPH along Gordon Road just before Martin Mill Road.  Ten houses sustained minor damage, mainly from falling trees and debris affecting the roof structures.  Although dozens of large trees were snapped or uprooted, evidence suggests the majority of the strongest winds remained slightly elevated, likely contributing to the lack of structural damage.  The tornado lifted as EF-0 along Martin Mill Road, just past the intersection of Gordon Road.||[01/21/12: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Coweta, 2012:001].

The Jackson County 911 Center reported a house fire sparked by lightning outside of Commerce.  The house was an old Victorian home that had been converted into apartments.  Seven residents escaped without injury, but the house was heavily damaged.

An EF-1 tornado touched down in Rome just west of the Maplewood Subdivision. EF-1 damage, consisting mostly of uprooted and snapped trees, occurred as the tornado moved in a general easterly direction.  The tornado traveled east of Rome and nearly paralleled Kingston Highway, where the most significant damage was sustained near the intersection of Kingston Highway and Freeman Ferry.  At this location, a small store lost a significant portion of its roof, and the entire roof was blown off of a single-wide manufactured home.  The one indirect fatality associated with the storm occurred at this location, when a 73-year-old woman died of a heart attack after the storm passed.  The tornado continued to parallel Kingston Highway, uprooting numerous trees.  A couple of outbuildings were damaged or destroyed due to falling trees, and a single-wide manufactured home was heavily damaged when a tree fell on it. The tornado weakened to an EF-0 and finally lifted just east of the intersection of Kingston Highway and Mathis Road.||[02/22/12: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Floyd, 2012:004].
The Madison County 911 Center relayed a first-responder report of nickel to quarter-sized hail in the Seagraves Mill Road area near the Madison/Jackson County Line.

The Jackson County 911 Center reported that nickel to quarter size hail fell from Hoschton to Jefferson between 11:50 PM and midnight.  Additional reports of heavy rain and large hail were received from the public through this area.
The public reported that nickel to quarter size hail occurred for approximately ten minutes in the Oakwood area.
The Troup County 911 Center reported nickel to golfball size hail occurring from near West Point to southeast of LaGrange.
A trained spotter reported that golf ball sized hail fell just north of Jewell.
The Morgan County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down near U.S. Highway 129 southeast of Madison.
The Greene County 911 Center reported that a few power lines were blown down along Willow Run Road.

The Jasper County 911 Center reported that more than a dozen trees were blown down from around Highway 83 South and Clay Road.  The straight-line wind damage continued to the south and southeast across unpopulated areas in the Oconee National Forest.  An additional 10 to 15 trees were blown down in the vicinity of Highway 11 and Clay Tillman Road northwest of Hillsboro.
The Talliaferro County 911 Center reported that a few trees and a few power lines were blown down near U.S. Highway 278.
The Putnam County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down along Route 129 and in Eatonton.  Traffic lights were were out in Eatonton as well.
The Warren County Emergency Manager reported that a couple of trees were blown down in Norwood and a few trees were blown down in Camak.

The Floyd County Emergency Manager reported that lightning struck a house on Morrison Campground Road.  The ensuing fire was quickly under control, only causing minor damage, mainly to the roof and attic of the house.

The Rockledge Post Office and the public reported nickel to quarter sized hail in a swath from Rocklege to near the Laurens/Treutlen County line.  Power was out in Rockledge.  A dog house sustained minor damage with the larger hail.
The Fayetteville FIre Department reported that a vacant home off Jasmine Court was struck by lightning and subsequently set on fire.  The home sustained moderate damage.
The public reported several downed trees across roads in Rockledge.
The Emanuel County 911 Center reported that golf ball sized hail occurred in Oak Park.
Floyd County Emergency Management relayed a trained spotter report of dime-sized hail on Morgan Valley Road.
The public reported golf ball sized hail in Acworth, south of Interstate 75 toward Sugar Maple Lane.
Floyd County Emergency Management relayed a report from a trained spotter of golf ball size hail near McGee Bend Road and Fosters Mill Road.
Cherokee County Emergency Management relayed a trained spotter report of quarter-sized hail just west of Woodstock.
Cherokee County Emergency Management reported quarter-sized hail northeast of Waleska.
The public reported penny-size hail in Calhoun.
Lightning struck a house near Campground Road and Major Road, catching the attic on fire.
The Fayette County Emergency Manager reported that lightning struck a residential structure on Osbourne Court, damaging the roof.

An EF-1 tornado touched down at approximately 8:09 PM in Haralson County near Cross Roads Church Road and Tallapoosa Highway, uprooting and snapping trees for several miles.  The tornado strengthened to an EF-3 along Bethlehem Church Road where a house collapsed and a repair shop was destroyed.  One person was injured when the house collapsed into the basement, where he was taking shelter.  At that residence, two dogs were killed.  A cow died in a nearby field.  The tornado continued across Haralson County, crossing Highway 27 where dozens of trees where snapped and uprooted.  As the tornado continued east, minor damage was sustained to a church where a steeple was blown off.  Hundreds of trees were down in forested areas in the eastern portions of Haralson County.  The tornado continued into Paulding County where it lifted near McClure Trail and McClure Drive around 8:50 PM.||[03/02/12: Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF3, Haralson, 2012:005].

The Haralson County tornado entered northwest Paulding County near Yorkville around 8:28 PM.  Numerous roads were closed due to debris.  Three miles south of Yorkville there was an overturned RV, and a box truck was impaled by a 2-by-4.  A residential neighborhood was hit, damaging several homes and destroying one.  The most significant damage occurred at the new Paulding County Regional Airport, where maximum wind speeds were estimated at near 135 MPH.  A hangar was destroyed and 19 of 23 planes were totaled, including a Citation jet.  Damage was sustained to the terminal and other airport property, such as fences and lamp posts, as well.  East of the airport, a church lost its roof.  Poole Elementary School had a partial roof failure and at least one wall blown out.  The portion of the roof that blew off was found across the campus.  Six modular classrooms were destroyed as well.  Additional homes were damaged as the tornado continued east, finally lifting near McClure Trail and McClure Drive around 8:50 PM.  The Georgia Emergency Management Agency reported that in Paulding County, 92 homes sustained minor damage, 58 sustained moderate damage, and 10 were destroyed. The total path length for both counties was 29 miles.||[03/02/12: Tornado #1, County #2-2, EF2, Paulding, 2012:005].

An EF-1 tornado with a maximum wind speed of 100 MPH touched down in Cobb County around 9:14 PM near East Cobb Park along Roswell Road.  It continued to track along Roswell Road where it caused roof damage to a daycare and a house near Providence Road.  Minor tree and roof damage continued just north of Roswell Road and ended near the Indian Ridge Subdivision around 9:15 PM.  The path length was just over a mile with a maximum width of 150 yards.||[03/02/12: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Cobb, 2012:006].
Amateur Radio operators relayed reports of several downed trees closing Interstate 24 in Dade County.
The DeKalb County 911 Center reported that several power lines were downed on DeKalb Industrial Way and Lawrenceville Highway.

Amateur Radio operators relayed multiple reports of hail from near the Polk/Haralson County line south of Cedartown, northeast toward Morgan Valley Road near Parham Springs Lake.  The hail ranged in size from dime to quarters.
Amateur Radio operators relayed reports of trees and power lines down in Rome, blocking the intersection of Highway 411 and Highway 27.
The Georgia Emergency Management Agency reported that several trees were downed in Alpharetta, causing minor, temporary road closures.

Numerous media outlets reported that an 83-year-old woman perished as an indirect result of the heavy rain. Family members indicated that she thought her interior closet unsafe in the event of a tornado, and that she wandered off just after midnight Saturday morning in search of a safer location. She sought shelter in a drainage ditch outside her home and was unable to escape when heavy rain caused the water to rise quickly.  Her body was found after daybreak Saturday morning, hundreds of yards away in a nearby creek.
The public reported hail up to the size of nickels in Nimblewill.

The public reported hail that lasted for at least 20 minutes in the area of Burnt Hickory Ridge Estates, northeast toward Harmony Grove Church Road.  The hail started as pea-size and grew to nickel-size by around 5:25 PM EDT.
The public reported that nickel-sized hail occurred at a location off Post Road.
The public reported quart-sized hail on Highway 278 about three miles west of Rockmart.

Floyd County Emergency Management and the public reported quarter-sized hail across southeastern Floyd County, from near Rockmart Road to near Shiflett and Pleasant Hope Roads.  The hail began as pea size and increased rapidly to quarter size, briefly accumulating.
A Bartow County 911 Center employee reported dime to quarter size hail at their residence on Erwin Hill Road, near the Gordon/Bartow County line.  The hail covered the lawn and car hoods.

The Middle Georgia Regional Airport manager reported nickel sized hail.  The weather observer at the airport reported that the hail lasted from 2:33 PM EDT and 2:40 PM EDT.

Numerous reports of pea to quarter size hail were received from Whitfield County Emergency Management and the public across the Tunnel Hill and Dalton areas.  Overall, the hail lasted for over 30 minutes as it varied in size.

Several reports were received from the public of quarter to golf ball size hail across portions of Gordon County from between Calhoun and Resaca southeast toward Sonoraville.  The large hail damaged several vehicles as well as windows to residences and businesses.

The Floyd County 911 Center reported that dime to quarter size hail fell in Rome and on the north side of Rome for about 10 minutes. The largest hail was on the north side of the city along Highway 27.

Trained spotters reported penny to quarter sized hail east to east-northeast of the Canton area.

The public reported quarter sized hail in Hiawassee.

A tornado touched down just southwest of Adairsville at approximately 1112 AM EST.  The tornado strengthened to high-end EF-3 in Adairsville where dozens of homes were damaged or destroyed.  At least 95 structures were damaged, with 31 destroyed, 17 sustaining major damage, and 47 with minor damage.  Most of the damage to homes was a result of trees falling on homes in downtown Adairsville.  The worst damage was along Highway 140 where a large portion of a manufacturing plant was destroyed.  One fatality occurred when a tree fell on a mobile home.  Over 100 cars were overturned near exit 306 on Interstate 75.|[01/30/13: Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF3, Bartow-Gordon, 2013:001].

The tornado that first touched down in Bartow County continued into Gordon County.  Numerous trees and power lines were downed from Redbud to Highway 53 and seven poultry homes were destroyed.  In all, 268 homes were impacted: 30 were completely destroyed, 110 had major damage, and another 70 had minor damage.  Of these, 202 were single family homes and 66 were mobile homes.  Eight injuries were also reported which all occurred in one home.  Some of the EF-3 damage in Gordon County occurred literally only blocks away from EF-3 damage that occurred on December 22, 2011.|[01/30/13: Tornado #1, County #2-2, EF3, Bartow-Gordon, 2013:001].

An EF-1 tornado touched down off of Chapman Drive and snapped or uprooted hundreds of softwood and hardwood trees as it moved northeast.  Eight power poles were snapped in the Bushyhead Road area.  Up to 12,000 people were without power.  Maximum wind speeds in Gilmer County were up to 90 MPH.  The tornado then moved into Fannin County.|[01/30/13: Tornado #2, County #1-2, EF1, Gilmer-Fannin, 2013:002].

The tornado that touched down in Gilmer County continued into Fannin County, moving northeast through the Sugar Creek area before lifting in the Hothouse Valley area.  The tornado with maximum wind speeds of 90 MPH snapped or uprooted hundreds of trees.  Up to 100 power poles were either snapped or damaged.  Thirty structures were damaged mainly due to falling trees.  While the maximum path width was about a half mile wide, the majority of the path was 300-400 yards wide.|[01/30/13: Tornado #2, County #2-2, EF1, Gilmer-Fannin, 2013:002].

The Rockdale County Sheriff's Office reported that a large pine tree fell on a pickup truck traveling on Interstate 20 between Sigman Road and the DeKalb County line, killing the occupant.  This accident resulted in a multiple-car pileup, as at least six other cars were involved in crashes as they tried to avoid the truck and the tree. The winds at the time were east at 15 to 20 MPH with gusts to 30 MPH and were associated with a wake low pressure gradient.  Saturated soils due to recent heavy rainfall contributed to the tree falling.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey determined that an EF-1 tornado touched down  northwest of Gibson.   Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted along the 1.5 mile path.  As the tornado crossed Georgia State Highway 171, it ripped off 20 percent of the metal roof from a home residence, tossed a camper trailer 50 feet, and knocked two mobile homes off their foundations.  The occupant of one home had to be rescued.  The worst damage occurred near the intersection of Georgia Highway 171 and Magnolia Church Road where 60 percent of the Magnolia Baptist Church roof was ripped off, and the brick-walled fellowship hall on the west end of the church was completely destroyed.  Numerous tombstones and other structures at the adjoining cemetery near the church were also damaged.|[03/05/13: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Glascock, 2013:003].

A home sustained minor roof damage, had both doors blown out, and four front windows were damaged.  One barn was completely destroyed, and another shifted several feet off its foundation.  A pontoon boat was thrown into a third barn.  Two neighboring houses sustained minor damage, one to the roof and another to the garage.  Thousands of trees were snapped or uprooted, some falling on homes.|[03/18/13: Tornado #1, County #2-2, EF2, Meriwether-Pike, 2013:004].

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF2 tornado with wind speeds up to 120 MPH touched down near Rocky Mount Road and Caldwell Road in Meriwether County.  IT traveled east to southeast before lifting one mile west of Concord in Pike County.  Total path length was 13.35 miles and up to 300 yards wide.  In Meriwether County, thousands of trees were either blown over or snapped, with some falling on homes.|[03/18/13: Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF2, Meriwether-Pike, 2013:004].

The Glascock County Emergency Manager reported that numerous trees and power lines were blown down from the Mitchell area to the Edgehill area.  Several large pines and at least one power pole were snapped.  Two homes were damaged by falling trees and several roads were blocked.  A tin roof was ripped off of a mobile home, and the south end of the county was without power.
The Marion County Emergency Manager reported that widespread dime-sized hail covered the ground along Georgia Highway 30.  Some of the hailstones were as large as golfballs.
The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported that golfball sized hail occurred in the Lithia Springs area, damaging vehicles and homes.
The Wilcox County 911 Center reported trees and power lines blown down county wide.

The Upson County 911 Center reported that trees and power lines were blown down county-wide, especially in the Yatesville area.  A mobile home was destroyed by a falling tree on Manley Road.  A vacant residence on Johnston Drive was damaged by a falling tree, and another home on Tom McKinley Road sustained roof and structural damage from a falling tree.  Numerous homes had shingle damage.  Farm equipment was blown over at The Rock Ranch.  Two to three chicken houses were blown apart.  A hangar door was blown off its tracks at the Thomaston-Upson airport.
The Washington County 911 Center reported trees and power lines blown down county wide.
The public reported that roof was blown off an auto sales store.
The Houston County Emergency Manager reported that widespread trees were down across the county.  Nearly all unincorporated areas were without power.
The Hancock County 911 Center reported numerous trees down across the county.
The Laurens County 911 Center reported that numerous trees were blown down across the county.
The Jones County 911 Center reported that numerous trees were blown down across the county.
The Harris County 911 Center reported numerous trees down near Whitesville.
The Monroe County Emergency Manager reported that trees were blown down countywide.  At least one car accident occurred as a result of the weather.
The Butts County Emergency Manager reported that numerous trees and power lines were blown down county wide.  Tree damage was especially heavy near Flovilla.
The Cherokee County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down or snapped in the Woodstock area.
Ham radio operators relayed a report of a tree down on a mobile home near Byron.
The ASOS station at the Macon airport measured a 52 kt gust.
The Harris County 911 Center reported numerous trees down throughout the county.

Ham radio operators and the Macon Fire Department reported wind damage across the Macon area.  Numerous trees and power lines were down across the city.  Several trees fell on homes, trapping the occupants inside.  Media also reported that the press box at the First Presbyterian Day School on Calvin Drive was blown over.

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that straight-line winds between 80 and 100 MPH occurred in the Silver Creek area.  A home off Center Road was damaged by winds approximately 80 MPH.  Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along Highway 101 where the Silver Creek Mini Mart was heavily damaged.  Winds were estimated at 100 MPH at this location.  Also, several homes were damaged due to falling trees.  Seven minor injuries occurred in the Silver Creek area, with three requiring hospitalization.
The public reported that numerous trees were blown down on Elders Mill Road.
The Coweta County Emergency Manager reported trees down across the northern part of the county.
The Polk County 911 Center relayed numerous reports of trees blown down or snapped with multiple power outages in the Cedartown area.  One tree fell on a car, injuring both occupants, one fatally.
The Floyd County Emergency Manager reported that numerous trees were blown down and snapped, with power outages, in the Rome area.
The Walker County 911 Center reported numerous trees blown down or snapped, with several power outages, in LaFayette.
The Chattooga County 911 Center reported that numerous trees were blown down or snapped, causing several power outages in Summerville.  Some of the trees fell on homes.
The Floyd County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down in the Cave Spring area.  Power lines fell on a vehicle on Padlock Mountain Road.
The Pike County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down in Hollonville, especially along Falcon Road.
The Middle Flint Regional E911 Center reported that several trees were blown down in Plains.

The Talbot County Sheriff's office reported that several trees were blown down near Georgia Highway 36.  At least one tree blocked a portion of the highway.  A motorist swerved to miss a tree that had fallen across the highway, subsequently hitting another tree.  The passenger was killed in the accident.
Broadcast media reported quarter sized hail in Norristown.
The Newton County 911 Center reported golfball sized hail in the Mansfield area.
The public and broadcast media reported large hail 1 to 2 inches in diameter across the Columbus area.  The hail fell for 10 minutes and covered the ground.
The public reported golfball sized  hail in Eatonton.  The hail was so deep it covered the ground completely.
