The public reported golfball size hail in McDonough.
The public reported 1 to 2 inch hail across southern Clayton County.
The Fayette County Emergency Manager and a storm chaser reported quarter to tennis ball sized hail in Fayetteville.
The Dawson County Emergency Manager reported quarter sized hail in Dawsonville.

Ham radio operators, spotters, and current and former National Weather Service employees reported golfball to baseball sized hail in Henry County in the first of two significant hailstorms to move through during the 6 PM hour.
The Meriwether County 911 Center relayed numerous reports of damage from baseball sized hail in Luthersville.

The Fulton County Emergency Manager as well as airline and federal employees at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport reported quarter to golfball sized hail at the airport.  Numerous windshields were broken on Interstate 85 south.
The public reported quarter sized hail in Union City.
The Coweta County Emergency Manager reported golfball sized hail in Grantville.
Ham radio operators relayed reports of golfball sized hail in Douglasville.
The public reported quarter sized hail just southeast of Waresville.
Ham radio operators and the public reported 1 to 2 inch hail across Carroll County in the second of two significant hailstorms that moved through.
The public reported quarter sized hail in Fort Oglethorpe.
Ham radio operators and the public reported quarter to half dollar sized hail in the first of two hailstorms to move across Carroll County.

The Henry County Emergency Manager, current and former National Weather Service Employees, and the public reported quarter to baseball sized hail in the second of two significant hailstorms across Henry County.

The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported that numerous trees and power lines were blown down in the Lithia Springs area.  Three vehicles and five homes were damaged by falling trees, and several roads were blocked.

The Haralson Gateway-Beacon reported that numerous trees and power lines were blown down from Tallapoosa to Bremen.  Several buildings in Tallapoosa sustained minor damage.  The Tally Mountain Golf Course had between 400-500 trees blown down and a fence and a porch destroyed.  In Bremen, several signs were damaged and a business sustained roof damage.
Parishioners at a local church and an employee of the Flat Creek Lodge reported several trees down on the east side of Summertown.
A trained spotter reported that a tree was blown down along Durham Street.
Employees at the Little Ocmulgee State Park reported that a few trees were blown down on the golf course.  A porch also had its roof blown off.
The Banks County Emergency Manager reported that an old chicken house and a barn sustained minor damage from strong winds along Carson Segars Road.  Several small trees were blown down as well.
The public reported nickel to quarter sized hail at McClain Farms.
The Johnson County Emergency Manager reported nickel sized hail.
The public reported quarter sized hail on the north side of Vidalia.

The public reported hail up to the size of pennies near Garfield.

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado touched down in Lumpkin County along Gold Ridge Road where numerous trees were snapped or uprooted.  One small outbuilding had its roof blown off and two homes sustained minor roof damage.  The tornado tracked northeast crossing Evergreen Court where trees were snapped and uprooted.  The tornado reached maximum intensity, around 105 MPH, shortly after and along Bridgestone Way where it paralleled the road.  Numerous hardwood and softwood trees were snapped and uprooted.  Some of the trees fell onto homes.  Twelve homes were damaged on Bridgestone Way, with two of them destroyed by trees.  The tornado then continued into Hall County.|[04/11/13: Tornado #3, County #1-3, EF1, Lumpkin-Hall-Lumpkin, 2013:007].

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that an EF-0 tornado touched down just south of Interstate 20 near Chandler Road.  The tornado continued northeast, crossing Kings Gin Road and along Thomas Road, snapping and uprooting several dozen trees.  Three homes on Kings Gin Road sustained minor roof damage where shingles or a portion of the roof was peeled back.  The tornado crossed Interstate 20, knocking over several trees on both east and westbound sides, just east of where Old Georgia 100 crosses the interstate.  The tornado continued across Dr. King Road and Petty Road, snapping and uprooting trees and just missing a large manufacturing center.  The tornado continued northeast and began to weaken as it headed across State Highway 100, Daniel Road, and U.S. Highway 78.  Several trees were uprooted and snapped along that path and a flower shop sustained minor roof damage at the intersection of U.S. Highway 78 and Old Ridgeway Road.  The tornado lifted shortly after crossing Highway 78.  |[04/11/13: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF0, Haralson, 2013:005].

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that a second brief tornado touched down associated with the same supercell thunderstorm as the Haralson County tornado.  The tornado touched down near railroad tracks just south of Coots Lake Road where some trees were uprooted.  From this point the tornado traveled to the north-northeast.  The most damage occurred in a wooded area 0.3 miles north of where the tornado touched down.  At this point approximately 50 trees were snapped and about 25 trees were uprooted.  The tornado dissipated in an open area just short of a residence.  Damage was confined to trees.|[04/11/13: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Polk, 2013:006].
The Whitfield County Emergency Manager reported a tree down on a house on Witherow Bridge Road.
The public reported several large trees blown down.  One fell on a house.
The Walker County Emergency Manager reported numerous trees down in Fort Oglethorpe.
The Murray County 911 Center reported numerous trees down in the Chatsworth area, particularly on the south side of town.
The Cherokee County Emergency Manager reported a tree down blocking a road near the Forsyth County line.
The Harris County 911 Center reported two trees were blown down across Highway 116.
The public reported multiple trees down on power lines on South Davis Road and Highway 27.
The Chattahoochee County 911 Center reported that a tree was blown down onto Highway 520 at Fort Benning.

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that the tornado that touched down in Lumpkin County crossed over into Hall County briefly.  It crossed Old Whelchel Road, snapping a few trees and downing powerlines.  Two homes sustained very minor roof damage.|[04/11/13: Tornado #3, County #2-3, EF1, Lumpkin-Hall-Lumpkin, 2013:007].

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that the tornado that touched down in Lumpkin County and crossed into Hall briefly crossed back into Lumpkin County.  It crossed Old Dahlonega Highway, damaging a few trees.  Two mobile homes were damaged by falling trees along Mount Olive Church Road, and several power lines were downed as well.  The tornado eventually weakened and lifted just before crossing Claude Perks Road and Starwood Drive.|[04/11/13: Tornado #1, County #3-3, EF1, Lumpkin-Hall-Lumpkin, 2013:007].
The Barrow County Emergency Manager and a local newspaper reported that several trees were blown down in Winder.
The Jackson County Emergency Manager reported that a few trees were blown down in Jefferson.
The Houston County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down in Warner Robins.  A couple fell on a house, causing roof damage.
Amateur radio operators reported that a tree fell on a house in Eatonton.
The Crisp County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down in the Cordele area.  Highway 41 was closed, and up to 2500 residents were without power.
Broadcast media reported that a tree fell on Highway 315 in Ellerslie.  A power line was blown down as well.

A  National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-2 tornado formed within a line of storms moving through Newton County.  It first touched down along Dukes Road, southwest of Mansfield, where it snapped and uprooted a few trees.  As the tornado moved east along Kellogg Street it increased in intensity, producing EF-1 damage to several homes along Kellogg Street and Savannah Street.  The EF-2 damage occurred to an older home on the north side of Kellogg Street where the home was completely destroyed.  A mobile home further east along Kellogg Street was also completely destroyed.  One person was injured in the mobile home and was trapped within the debris.  Numerous trees and power lines were snapped and downed along Kellogg Stret as well as further east along Sewell and Lloyd Roads.  In all, eight homes sustained significant damage and a few buildings in downtown Mainsfield sustained minor damage.  The tornado began to weaken as it headed northeast crossing CR-213 where a park sustaned damage to several outbuildings and several trees were uprooted.  Minor tree damage was noted in the town of Newborn as the tornado moved through the north side of town.  The tornado then crossed into Morgan County.|[04/19/13: Tornado #1, County #1-2, EF2, Newton-Morgan, 2013:008].

The tornado that touched down in Newton County crossed into Morgan County briefly.  The track ended near the intersection of Durden Road and Reese Road where a few trees were snapped and uprooted.|[04/19/13: Tornado #1, County #2-2, EF2, Newton-Morgan, 2013:008].
The Chattooga County Emergency Manager reported that a tree was blown down across Highway 48 near Ridge Street.
The Talbot County Sheriff's office reported that two trees were blown down in Woodland, one along Highway 36 and another along Highway 208.
The Houston County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were blown down in the Bonaire area.
Broadcast media relayed a report of several trees blown down along Highways 96 and 358 in southern Twiggs County.

A National Weather Service storm survey confirmed that straight-line wind damage with estimated winds of 80 to 90 MPH resulted in dozens of trees down and uprooted with large limbs twisted off.  One tree was blown down through a house and another on a car.  Glass was blown out of a Circle-K store with part of the roof blown off.  A restaurant along victory drive suffered damage to the building and a sign out front.  Three traffic lights were blown down.   Most of the damage ocucrred near the intersection of Elm Drive, Macon Road, and University Avenue.
Several reports were relayed from the public of quarter to baseball sized hail in the LaGrange area.  Damage was reported to windows, cars and roofs.
The public reported golf ball sized hail across Covington.
The public reported quarter sized hail in Covington.
The Wilkes County 911 Center reported quarter sized hail southwest of Washington.
The broadcast media relayed a report of four trees down in Oglethorpe.  One tree fell on a car.
The Crawford County Emergency Manager relayed a report of four trees down in the southern part of the county.
The broadcast media relayed reports of a tree down in Warner Robins.
The Greene County Emergency Manager relayed a report of a tree down near Union Point.
The Wilkes County Emergency Manager relayed a report of a tree and several power lines down on Troke Drive off Highway 47.

A National Weather Service and Emergency Management survey team determined an EF-0 tornado with maximum winds of 85 MPH briefly touched down just east of Moreland near Martin Mill Road and Windom Drive where a 35X35 ft outbuilding used as a workshop was destroyed. A 20 ft pontoon boat and 30 ft camper trailer were thrown about 50 yards and destroyed. The adjacent home sustained minor damage to its patio and roof. Light debris was thrown up to 150 yards. Six medium sized trees were damaged, snapped or uprooted, some of which showed signs of rot.|[04/28/13: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF0, Coweta, 2013:009].
A National Weather Service employee reported a large oak tree down along Georgia Highway 20 northeast of McDonough.

A National Weather Service survey team determined that a weak EF-0 tornado touched down at Turner Church Road and North Ola Road. A tree was downed at that location. The tornado then lifted and touched down in the Sleepy Hollow subdivision where most of its damage occurred. Five houses had damaged siding, six trees were downed and an outbuilding had damage to its roof. The tornado lifted just east of the subdivision. Eyewitnesses reported rotation and that they received the warning in plenty of time to seek shelter.|[04/28/13: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF0, Henry, 2013:010].
The Dade County Emergency Manager reported that multiple trees were blown down across the county.
The Washington County 911 Center reported multiple trees down across the county.

The Wilscot Creek flooded around six different roads with up to two feet of water and damaged two county bridges and three private bridges. Portions of Old Dial Road were affected the most with a camper being washed away and getting crushed under a bridge. Rapid flowing flood waters caused a propane tank to break away from a house and float downstream. The flooding also surrounded and entered a house which temporarily stranded an elderly couple. A land slide occurred on a portion of Daves Road.

County officials reported that Anderson and Coosa Creeks flooded the Mountain Oak Cabins and Campground area around 3.5 miles southwest of Blairsville. The RV park was flooded in low lying areas with a few vacation homes inundated with water. A few culverts were washed out. The Youngcane and Jones Creeks flooded portions of Byers Road around 7 miles west of Blairsville. The flood waters topped the bridge and caused erosion damage to it.

The USGS stream gage on the Etowah River reached flood stage of 13 feet. The river crest at 15.9 feet. Moderate flooding occurred with several road closures. Etowah River Road was completely washed out where the dirt portion of it parallels the river. The road is expected to be closed for the next 2 weeks for repairs. A landslide occurred on a portion of Georgia Highway 53 near War Hill Park Road. Two feet of mud covered one lane with only one lane passable.

Trudy Drive was completely washed out by a drainage branch flowing into Lake Lanier. There was a 50 to 75 foot large gap in the road with at least a 10 foot drop off. Several other roads were closed and damaged by flood waters as drainage branches become rapidly flowing creeks and overwhelmed culverts. These roads included portions of Atlanta Highway, McEver Road, Stephens Road, Flowery Way, Spring Street and Cove Creek Road in the Flowery Branch area.

The USGS stream gage on Dick Creek at Old Atlanta Road near Johns Creek and Suwanee reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 12.8 feet. Minor flooding occurred with a few road closures nearby.
The USGS stream gage on the Big Creek at Atlanta Highway near Cumming reached flood stage of 6 feet. The creek crest at 8.2 feet. Minor flooding occurred along the Big Creek Greenway.

The USGS stream gage on Level Creek at Suwanee Dam Road near Sugar Hill and Suwanee reached flood stage of 9 feet. The creek crest at 13 feet. Moderate flooding occurred with the water level hitting the bridge and reaching the bottom of the USGS gage house. Also the USGS stream gage on Richland Creek at Suwanee Dam Road near Sugar Hill and Buford reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 10.5 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and residential yards along the creeks.

The USGS stream gage on the Big Creek at Kimball Bridge Road near Alpharetta reached flood stage of 7 feet. The creek crest at 10.3 feet. Minor flooding occurred. The USGS stream gage on the Chattahoochee River near Berkeley Lake and Norcross reached flood stage of 12 feet. The river crest at 12.4 feet. Minor flooding occurred. The Chattahoochee River rose out of its banks and flooded the paddocks and access road to the stables at the Huntcliff River Club near Sandy Springs. Emergency officials evacuated 20 horses from the stables.

The USGS stream gage on Pew Creek at Patterson Road near Lawrenceville reached flood stage of 11 feet. The creek crest at 14.3 feet. Moderate flooding occurred and the water level hit the bridge for around one hour. The USGS stream gage on Suwanee Creek at Buford Highway near Suwanee reached flood stage of 8 feet. The creek crest at 11.8 feet. Moderate flooding occurred with several road closures nearby. The USGS stream gage on Sweetwater Creek at Club Drive near Liburn reached flood stage of 11 feet. The creek crest at 13.1 feet. Minor flooding occurred. Long lake overflowed and flooded parts of the Riverbrooke neighborhood near Duluth. Backyards were flooded and the water came close to the houses.

Significant flooding occurred northwest through northeast of Trion on Chattooga Creek, Cane Creek, Chappel Creek and Spring Branch which caused minor flooding downstream on the Chattooga River in Summerville. The emergency manager reported up to 20 roads were closed in this area due to overflowing creeks. Six mobile homes were flooded and abandoned. First responders had difficulty in reaching 15 people in the mobile homes for evacuation near U.S. Highway 27 at the intersection of West and East Halls Valley Roads. Some major erosion occurred on portions of the roads.
The public reported several small creeks came out of their banks and briefly flooded portions of nearby roads in the Cooper Heights area.

The public reported several roads in the Adairsville area with high water overflowing them from nearby drainage branches. This included Clear Deck Road, Mathews Road and East Pleasant Valley Road around 5 to 6 miles east to southeast of Adairsville.
The emergency manager reported numerous drainage branches and small creeks in the Rome area overflowed their banks. This affected low lying portions of 15 roads which caused temporary road closures.

The public reported several drainage branches and small creeks from Rockmart to near Taylorsville overflowed their banks. This affected low lying portions of a few roads which caused temporary road closures.

The emergency manager reported a small creek overflowed a portion of McKown Road around 4 miles east to northeast of Douglasville. The culvert pipe was washed out with significant erosion damage to the road.
The emergency manager reported Mill Creek had overflowed low lying portions of Willowdale Road near Chattanooga Road. The road was temporarily closed.

The emergency manager reported several drainage branches and small creeks overflowed their banks and flooded low lying portions of several roads from Cole City to Wildwood and Morganville. A family was stranded in their home near Cole City by surrounding flood waters.  First responders had a difficult time reaching them to evacuate to higher ground.

The USGS stream gage on Lookout Creek at Creek Road near New England and Trenton reached flood stage of 12 feet. The creek crest at 16.7 feet. Significant flooding occurred near the moderate flood stage of 17 feet with several road closures.

The public reported several roads in the Adairsville area with high water overflowing them from nearby drainage branches. This included Clear Deck Road, Mathews Road and East Pleasant Valley Road around 5 to 6 miles east to southeast of Adairsville.

The Carroll County Emergency Manager reported a couple of trees down.  Pea sized hail was also reported.

The Coweta County 911 Center relayed a report of quarter size hail along North Highway 29 near Greentop Road.

The Meriwether County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down in eastern Meriwether County, specifically along Gay Road near Murray Road and along Highway 100 near mile marker 10.

The Upson County 911 Center reported several trees and power lines down across roads on the north side of Thomaston.  A few other trees were reported down in the eastern part of the county.
The Upson County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a house on the north side of Thomaston.  The house caught fire but the fire was quickly extinguished.
The Upson County 911 Center reported that several trees were blown down in the Yatesville area of eastern Upson County.
The public reported that at least 15 large trees were uprooted or snapped along Quail Ridge Road.
The Gwinnett Times reported that a large tree was blown down, which broke five to six power poles.
The Gwinnett Times reported that a tree was down on Interstate 85 near Buford Drive.
The Carroll County Emergency Manager reported that a couple of trees were blown down in Whitesburg.
An amateur radio operator reported that nickel sized hail fell near Hog Mountain.
An amateur radio operator reported that a tree fell on a house near Hog Mountain, causing damage to the back of the house.
A trained spotter reported that a power line was blown down on MacLand Road near Hiram.
Local newspaper reported that several trees and power lines were blown down in the Lawrenceville area.
Local newspaper reported that several trees and power lines were reported down in the Loganville area.
Local newspaper reported that several trees were blown down between Highways 138 and 92 east of Fairburn toward Jonesboro Road.
Broadcast media reported that several trees were blown down in Butler.

Amateur radio operators reported that a few trees were blown down in Montezuma.  One fell on power lines along north Dooly Street, another was on Old Perry Road, and another on Highway 127 on Marvis Chapman Road.
The Crisp County Emergency Manager reported around 10 trees down across the east and southeast portions of the county, mainly east of Interstate 75.
The public reported penny sized hail in Sandersville.
The public reported nickel sized hail in Wrens.
The public reported quarter sized hail in Jackson.
The Bibb County 911 Center reported trees down along High Street.
Broadcast media relayed a report of a downed tree on Mock Springs Road.
A trained spotter reported several trees down on Highway 278 east of Greensboro.
The Peach County Emergency Manager reported dime to penny sized hail.
The public reported quarter to half dollar sized hail in McDonough.
Broadcast media relayed reports of a few trees down near Between, just east of Loganville.
Broadcast media relayed reports of several trees down in yards in Duluth; none fell on houses.
The public reported several trees either blown down or snapped.
A trained spotter measured a wind speed of 53.5 MPH.  Two large pine trees were snapped and trash cans were blown more than 100 feet down the road.
The White County 911 Center reported that a tree was blown down on Highway 129.
The Banks County Emergency Manager reported a tree down on Apple Pie Ridge Road.
The Wilkinson County Deputy Emergency Manager reported several trees down from near Clear Creek Baptist Church on Highway 18 to Dedrick Road.
The Jackson County Emergency Manager reported several trees down just northwest of Jefferson.
The Taylor County Emergency Manager reported three trees down near Reynolds.
The Crawford County Emergency Manager reported a couple of trees down on the south end of the county.
The Houston County Emergency Manager reported three trees down on Collins Road.

The Middle Flint Regional E911 Center reported that structural damage occurred to a chicken house off of Garden Valley Road, and there was some roof damage to a mobile home in Ideal.  A few trees and some power lines were blown down and snapped off Plantation Road, and a few large trees were blown down blocking roads and causing power outages in Ideal.

Intense heavy rainfall of 3.23 inches in 100 minutes at the Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport caused significant flooding on portions of Interstate 285 at the Camp Creek Parkway intersection. Several cars stalled out in the flood waters.

A USGS stream gage on North Fork Peachtree Creek at Buford Highway reached flood stage of 13 feet. The creek crest at 13.7 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the backyards of residential homes along the creek.
Portions of at least 6 roads in the Dexter, Cadwell and Rentz areas had 6 inches or more of flowing water over the roads from nearby ditches and small streams.

A USGS stream gage on Nancy Creek at Johnson Ferry Road reached flood stage of 16 feet. The creek crest at 16.2 feet. This caused minor flooding in the woodlands along the creek and on the athletic fields of the Marist High School campus. Flooding of residential yards occurred also.

Intense heavy rain caused a dam breach of a 7 acre pond by Roswell Road. An access road over the dam was the only entrance into a neighborhood which is now cutoff. Erosion caused severe damage to the access road.

Around 3.5 inches of rain in less than 3 hours caused a pond to overflow Sunset Blvd. Rapidly flowing water caused severe erosion and dug a six foot deep hole in front of a culvert pipe on Grandchester Way.

Hurricane Branch overflowed a portion of Oaky Grove Church Road with around one foot of water. Cypress Creek overflowed a portion of Powerline Road with around one foot of water. A drainage branch overflowed a portion of Carters Road near Georgia Highway 15 with around one foot of water.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Point Fire burned 0.1 acres and resulted in $250 in damages.
Brier creek around 5 miles east of Warrenton overflowed a portion of East Warrenton Road with up to one foot of water.
Several farm ponds in the southeast area of Carroll County overflowed causing minor erosion damage to the dams and briefly flooding nearby roads downstream.
A farm pond in northwest Coweta County overflowed and briefly flooded a portion of Adcock Road.

Heavy rain overwhelmed the storm drains in Watkinsville and caused flood waters to enter the basement of a church at the corner of Main Street and Simonton Bridge Road. The water got up to one foot deep in the basement. There appeared to be no debris blockage contributing to the flooding.
The National Forest Service reported that a wildfire of unknown cause labeled Shooting Range burned 0.1 acres and resulted in $300 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Callihan Road burned 0.25 acres and resulted in $1,500 in damages.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Turnpike Creek at U.S. Highways 319 and 441 reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 10.1 feet with minor flooding of woodlands and fields. The emergency manager reported a couple of road closures in the central portion of the county due to water covering roadways.

Flood waters from several creeks in central Coweta County affected a few athletic areas including the soccer fields off of Georgia Highway 34. The White Oak Creek flooded portions of the Summergrove Golf Course and the water reached the garage of a home on the east side of Newnan.
A couple of creeks were temporarily out of their banks and caused two roads to be closed due to flooding in a portion of central Haralson County.

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that an EF-1 tornado touched down near the intersection of Patriot Trail and Rampley Trail, causing mainly tree damage as it headed southeast toward Canton.  Along Marietta Road and Hickory Flat Highway, a Chevron gas station sustained roof damage, and a gas pump was blown over.  Dozens of trees were snapped or uprooted.  The tornado then headed south-southeast causing additional tree damage, lifting near the intersection of New Light Road and Hickory Road.  Two minor injuries occurred in Canton as a result of trees falling.|[06/13/13: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Cherokee, 2013:011].

A National Weather Service survey team determined that a second tornado touched down just within a tenth of a mile of the Cherokee-Cobb County line along Woodhaven Drive.  Trees and large limbs were reported down at this location before the tornado moved into Cobb County.|[06/13/13: Tornado #2, County #1-3, EF1, Cherokee-Cobb-Fulton, 2013:012].

The tornado that touched down just inside the Cherokee County line moved into Cobb County and strengthened to an EF-1.  The tornado tracked southeast through Cobb County with the most significant damage occurring near Wendwood Drive Northeast and near Bishop Lake where dozens of trees were snapped and uprooted, many causing damage to homes.  The tornado continued to track southeast, and crossed the Chattahoochee River at the Cobb-Fulton County line near the Morgan Falls Dam.|[06/13/13: Tornado #2, County #2-3, EF1, Cherokee-Cobb-Fulton, 2013:012].

A National Weather Service storm survey team determined that the tornado that began in Cherokee County and passed through Cobb County lifted in Fulton County.  It moved over the Chattahoochee River near Morgan Falls, retaining its EF-1 strength as it snapped and uprooted dozens of trees along the riverbank.  It damaged roofs at the Laurel at Overlook Park Apartments.  Netting polls at the driving range at the Steel Canyon Golf Club were damaged, with the netting ripped off or tangled.  The tornado continued southeast, snapping or uprooting trees until it finally lifted just short of the DeKalb County line, where it snapped and uprooted a few trees along Twin Branch Road.|[06/13/13: Tornado #2, County #3-3, EF1, Cherokee-Cobb-Fulton, 2013:012].

A National Weather Service survey team determined that an EF0 tornado touched down just inside the Georgia-Alabama state line in Heard County.  A mobile home sustained roof damage and its porch was destroyed as the tornado tracked northeastward, paralleling Upper Caldwell Road as it strengthened to an EF1.  The most significant damage was as the tornado crossed Upper Caldwell Road, snapping dozens of trees.  The tornado left a path 0.4 miles in length, weakening back to an EF0 with tree limbs down before it lifted.  |[08/18/13: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Heard, 2013:013].

The Middle Georgia EMC reported a few power outages across the county, mainly in the south and southwest portion, mostly caused by downed limbs.  The Wilcox County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were blown down in Pitts as well.

The Johnson County Emergency Manager reported trees and power lines down on Tucker Grove Church Road, Georgia Highway 57, U.S. Highway 319, Old Buckeye Road, and New Buckeye Road.
The Laurens County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down along Buckeye Road.

The Barrow County Emergency Manager reported that nine trees were blown down, and two of them on houses.  One of the trees on a house was on Nunnally Road, and the other on Soloman Drive.  A resident on Nunnally Road had minor injuries, and the Red Cross was called for the Soloman Drive residence.

The Jackson County Emergency Manager estimated 75-80 trees were blown down, mainly in the Jefferson and Arcade area.  Ten houses were damaged, most due to falling trees, but a couple had windows blown out due to the strong winds.  Multiple power lines were down as well.  Most of the damage was along Jett Roberts Road into downtown Jefferson and along Johnson Mill Road in Arcade.

Broadcast media relayed a report of a tree down on a house in Manchester.

The Gwinnett County Emergency Manager reported that lightning started a house fire on White Blossom Lane.
The Gwinnett County Emergency Manager reported that lightning started a small fire at a house on Lakeshore Drive.
The public reported a small creek rapidly rising and out of its banks behind homes on Jewel Court in the Guilford Forest area. Minor flooding occurred in the residential backyards.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage on the Nickajack Creek at Veterans Memorial Highway near Mableton reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 10.3 feet. Minor flooding occurred in portions of Nickajack Park upstream from the gage.

The Atlanta local media and Hall County emergency manager confirmed a portion of C. Rogers Road near White Sulpher in north Hall County was washed out due to a culvert pipe being overwhelmed by flood waters from localized intense rainfall.  The washed out road caused around 100 families to become isolated with no other alternative route.
The public reported drainage ditches and a farm pond overflowed a portion of Raford Wilson Road just northwest of Jefferson. Some minor erosion damage occurred.

The Pickens County Fire Department evacuated a man from a manufactured home off Wigington Lane north of Jasper due to a creek beginning to flood on the property. The flood waters damaged a car in front of the house and entered the home.

The Pickens County emergency manager reported swift water rescues in progress at Sharptop Cove Young Life Camp off of Camp Hope Road northeast of Jasper. A portion of the road was washed out by Long Swamp Creek which was cutting off the camp. Two camp employees in a truck attempted to cross the flood waters and were washed downstream around 40 yards from the culvert. A portion of Tamarack Drive was completely washed out by the same creek around one quarter mile downstream from the camp. Another swift water rescue and evacuation from a home was in progress off of Price Creek Trail. Flood waters from Price Creek were threatening the home and first responders were having difficulty reaching the home due to a washed out road. A landslide around 100 feet wide and around 40 feet high closed one lane on a portion of Georgia Highway 136. In summary, 3 evacuations and 3 swift water rescues of people occurred.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage near Talking Rock on Fausett Creek at Yukon Road reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 15.3 feet with significant flooding. Some erosion around the concrete box culvert under the road occurred. This was the second highest crest in the gage history for this location.

The Gilmer County emergency manager reported a swift water rescue occurred at a home on Avery Drive in the Talona area. Several creeks in southeast Gilmer County such as Clear...Price...Fausett and Turkey Creeks flooded and washed out some roads and a few bridges. Multiple swift water rescues occurred with several evacuations of homes due to rapidly rising flood waters. Around 8 roads were either washed out or damaged...one bridge was washed out at Holt Road...around 25 structures were flooded with some washed off their foundations...8 people needed swift water rescues and 10 people were evacuated from structures. The Mountain Valley Farm Store and two large chicken houses off of Homer Wright Road were flooded and heavily damaged. It was estimated around 170,000 chickens were killed. The Georgia EPD condemned the area and had the chickens destroyed and properly buried.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage on the Cartecay River near East Ellijay reached flood stage of 7 feet. The river crest at 10.2 feet causing significant flooding. The Gilmer County emergency manager indicated around 7 roads were either flooded or damaged in the East Ellijay area by high water from the Cartecay River. Around 25 structures were flooded with some evacuations on White Water Lane, Bernhardt Road, River Lane and Riverside Drive. The East Ellijay Police Chief was injured by electric shock during an evacuation on Riverside Drive. A power line fell on the patrol car as it was passing through the flooded road. He was hospitalized and released a day or two later.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage near Ellijay on the Coosawattee River off of Legion Road reached flood stage of 8 feet. The river crest at 9 feet which caused minor flooding of portions of Harold Hefner River Park.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage on the Etowah River at Georgia Highway 9 south of Dawsonville reached flood stage of 13 feet. The river crest at 15.3 feet and caused minor flooding of river access roads...woodlands and fields.
Dawson County officials reported Yellow Creek was out of it banks and flowing over the bridge on Holcomb Road. A portion of Holcomb Road was closed.

The Forsyth County emergency manager reported a drainage branch flowing into Fourmile Creek just west of Chestatee was overflowing a portion of Grindle Road. The road was closed due to flooding just north of Georgia Highway 306.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Talking Rock Creek near Hinton reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 11.8 feet causing minor flooding of creek access roads and woodlands.
An off duty NWS employee reported the Sullivan Branch was out of its banks and caused minor flooding on the Summergrove golf course.

The White County emergency manager reported Brasstown Creek came out of it banks and flooded a portion of Puddlebee Road around 6 miles northeast of Cleveland. A barn nearby was also flooded with animals stranded. The same creek further downstream flooded a portion of Roy Powers Road.

The White County emergency manager reported that Shoal Creek and its associated drainage branches in southwest White County came out of their banks and flooded portions of Georgia Highway 115 and 284. Water was up to 8 inches deep over parts of Georgia Highway 115 and 284 with a couple of culverts washed out.

Muscogee County officials reported the Cooper Creek Reservoir around 5 miles northeast of Columbus was overflowing and flooding Cooper Creek downstream from the dam. At least four roads were affected by flood waters and closed such as Fairview Drive, Roland Avenue, Northgate Drive and Reese Road. Flood waters entered a home in the Northgate subdivision and heavily damaged culvert pipes under residential driveways.

The Laurens County Police reported several roads under water around 2 miles southwest of Dublin. A drainage branch was overflowing a portion of Southern Pines Road near U.S. Highway 441. Also several cars were reported partially submerged by the local media.

The Houston County emergency manager reported flood waters from drainage ditches and small streams overflowed portions of around 10 roads in the Centerville area. Some minor flooding of a few residential yards near the streams occurred. The flood waters flowed into the Bay Gall Creek basin.

The Toombs County emergency manager reported flood waters from nearby creeks and streams overflowed portions of around 6 roads in the English Eddy area. This included portions of Georgia Highway 147 and Cedar Crossing Road.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Little River at Georgia Highway 16 reached flood stage of 20 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands...fields and dirt access roads along the river.

The Upson County emergency manager reported a stream that flows into Bell Creek overflowed its banks and flooded a portion of MLK Jr Drive and Walton Street in the Lincoln Park neighborhood south of Thomaston.

The Crisp County Deputy emergency manager reported several small creeks and streams came out of their banks and flooded portions of some roads in eastern crisp county. The soils were wet from previous rainfall during the past 30 days.

The DeKalb County emergency manager reported the South Fork Peachtree Creek came out of its banks and caused minor flooding near Orion Drive and Lawrenceville Highway. The same creek also flooded portions of Medlock Park and athletic fields with up to 3 feet of water. Three homes on Scott Circle near the creek had flood waters enter their crawl spaces. A portion of Snapfinger Creek came out of its banks and flooded a home on Rowland Road with around one inch of water.  The stage height at a USGS stream gage on Stone Mountain Creek at Silver Hill Road reached flood stage of 9 feet. The creek crest at 9.1 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and residential yards along the creek.

The White County emergency manager reported a few rapid responding creeks in the Cleveland area came out of their banks and overflowed portions of some roads. The roads were closed for around two hours.

Dawson County officials reported several drainage branches and streams were flooding portions of roads primarily north and southeast of Dawsonville. Some of the roads included Grizzle Road, Harry Sosebee Road, Tanner Hall Road, Blacks Mill Road and Nix Bridge Road. A house and car were damaged by flood waters in the 2700 block of Lumpkin Campground Road.

Washington County officials reported a stream flowing into the Little Ohoope River near Pringle overflowed its banks and affected portions of New Bethel Road and Bartow-Dublin Road with minor flooding.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Big Creek at Atlanta Highway 6 miles southwest of Cumming reached flood stage. The creek crest around 6 feet. Minor flooding occurred on large portions of the sidewalks and boardwalks of the Big Creek Greenway.
The Catoosa County 911 Center reported several trees down, including along Highway 41, Salem Valley Road, and Dogwood Road.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Hwy 286 burned 3.4 acres and resulted in $1000 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Dry Creek burned 0.1 acres and resulted in $3000 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Little Amy Creek burned 2.5 acres and resulted in $7000 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Stateline burned 6.7 acres and resulted in $6200 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Charlie's Creek burned 3.1 acres and resulted in $3300 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Little Mountaintown Trail burned 5 acres and resulted in $2850 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Yeti burned 3 acres and resulted in $2500 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled River Ridge burned 1 acre and resulted in $1200 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled FLT burned 0.1 acres and resulted in $200 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Deavers Road burned 1.23 acres and resulted in $450 in damages.
The National Forest Service reported that a human-caused wildfire labeled Boling Knob burned 7.31 acres and resulted in $800 in damages.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Intrenchment Creek at Constitution Road reached flood stage of 11 feet. The creek crest at 11.2 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and natural flood plain along the creek.

The stage height of a USGS stream gage on the North Fork Peachtree Creek at Buford Highway reached flood stage of 13 feet. The creek crest at 13.1 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the low portions of residential backyards off of Victory Drive, Dunwoody Place and Converse Drive.
The broadcast media reported 50 to 60 MPH winds in Vinings.
A trained spotter reported a 64 MPH wind gust with tree limbs down.
The Jefferson County Emergency Manager reported a tree down in Wrens.
Amateur radio operators reported numerous trees down in the Sandersville area.  Power was out in some parts of town as well.
A trained spotter reported multiple trees down in Irwinton, as well as trees down east of Irwinton along Highway 57.
The Twiggs County 911 Center reported 10 trees down across the county.
A trained spotter reported two trees down on Sandefur Road near Houston Lake Road and another tree down at Lake Joy Road and Sandefur Road.
The Crawford County Emergency Manager reported that a porch was blown off the front of a home on Jackson Road.  Several trees were blown down in the county as well.

The Coweta County 911 Center reported that trees were down at South Highway 29 and Lowery Road, the 4700 block of Corinth Road and mile marker 34 on Interstate 85 South.  Also, a power line was down on Willow Lake Road and East Highway 34.
The Banks County Emergency Manager reported that a tree and a couple of lines were down at Damascus and Prospect Roads.
The Fulton County Emergency Manager reported that numerous trees were blown down in Milton.
The Hall County 911 Center reported that 10 trees and power lines were blown down across the eastern portion of the county.
The Rockdale County Emergency Manager reported that a tree was blown down at Ebenezer and Troupe Smith Roads.
The Hall County 911 Center reported that 10 trees were blown down across the western portion of the county.
The Heard County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were blown down south of Roopville.
The Cherokee County Emergency Manager reported that several trees were blown down in an area west of Woodstock.  One tree fell on a home, trapping and injuring two occupants.
The Cherokee County 911 Center reported that numerous trees were down across the southern portion of the county.  Several were down at the intersection of Highway 140 and East Cherokee Drive.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey determined that straight-line winds of 80 MPH struck the Floyd-Polk Medical Center in Cedartown.  The winds lifted the vinyl awning off the hospital entrance and pulled some of the metal support beams from the concrete base.  These metal support beams punctured the roof and allowed the rain to enter the building through the holes.  This water caused damage to the interior of the structure.  In addition, some of the debris hit cars parked near the building and damaged six vehicles.  A small portion of the metal roof on a nearby building was peeled back.  A few limbs were down near the medical center and two business signs nearby were damaged.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey determined that a brief EF-0 tornado touched down in Cherokee County.  Although the total path length was three miles, the tornado skipped along the ground with sporadic damage.  Several trees were downed along a path that stretched from 1.75 miles northeast of Waleska to 4.5 miles northeast of Waleska.  In addition to the downed trees, a fence near the starting point of the tornado was damaged when a tree fell on it.|[01/11/14: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF0, Cherokee, 2014:001].
The public reported hail up to the size of quarters.
The Dawson County 911 Center reported that a couple of trees were blown down in Dawsonville.
An off-duty NWS employee reported that several trees were blown down along Highway 85 near Sara Harp Minter Elementary School.

Overall, heavy snow across north Georgia, generally north of the Metropolitan Atlanta area but south of the highest elevations of the north Georgia mountains, accumulated to widespread amounts of 2 to 4, with isolated higher reports up to 5 inches.  Most of this fell with the first round of precipitation.

A significant winter storm impacted north and portions of central Georgia on Tuesday the 11th and Wednesday the 12th. For areas south of the Atlanta Metropolitan area and into central Georgia, the event began Wednesday morning the 12th.  Rain mixed with and changed over to freezing rain through the morning hours, resulting in ice accretions of a tenth (0.1) to a third (0.33) of an inch of ice.  Widespread power outages were reported, with some customers without power for over two days.  The event ended as a round of light snow Wednesday evening.

The AWOS site KMGE in Marietta measured a 50 kt gust.
The Macon broadcast media relayed a report of a tree down along Sugarloaf Circle.

Broadcast media and the public reported multiple trees down in the Marietta area, including West Paces Ferry Road, Windy Hill Road, and Lower Roswell Road.  At the intersection of Oak Knoll Drive and Cross Gate Drive, multiple trees were down, including one that fell on a home and injured a child.
A National Weather Service storm survey determined that straight-line winds snapped two trees and uprooted five other, with several branches down in the area as well.
The Gilmer County 911 Center reported that a tree was blown down along Zion Hill Road.
The Floyd County 911 Center reported that several trees and power lines were blown down in and around the Rome area.

The Walker County 911 Center reported that multiple trees were blown down in LaFayette, including along Broomtown Road, Glass Road, Straightgut Road, Dipping Springs Road, Highway 136, Garretts Chapel Road and Boss Road.
The Catoosa County 911 Center reported multiple trees down in and near Ringgold, including along Holcomb Road, Old Tunnel Road, Smith Chapel Road, LaFayette Road and Highway 41.
The Dade County 911 Center reported that a tree was down on a house on Newsome Gap Road, trapping the resident inside.

A National Weather Service survey team determined that an EF0 anticyclonic tornado touched down near the Dodge County Hospital off Plaza Avenue, initially uprooting trees and peeling back the roof of a nursing home. A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 107 MPH, touched down in southwest Monroe County and moved northeast across the county before lifting near Juliette. Extensive tree damage was noted along the path with many trees snapped and uprooted. The tornado reached its peak intensity as it crossed Reedy Creek Road where several large hardwood trees were snapped. A barn collapsed at this location and another had its metal roof peeled off. A shed was destroyed and a tree fell on a house in Smarr. [11/23/14: Tornado #6, County #1-1, EF1, Monroe, 2014:023].

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 100 MPH, touched down on Highway 26 near Loggins Road where it ripped shingles off of a house and destroyed an above-ground pool. The tornado reached its peak intensity along Pitts Road where a tied-down double-wide mobile home was pushed off of its foundation and had its roof peeled off. On East Flournoy Road a shed was overturned, trees were snapped and a boat was tossed over one hundred feet into a cotton field. Windows were blown out of a house at this location as well. [11/23/14: Tornado #9, County #1-2, EF1, Houston-Pulaski, 2014:026].

A NWS storm survey team determined that the tornado that touched down in Houston county moved into Pulaski County causing EF-0 damage with maximum wind speeds of 75 MPH. Trees were snapped and uprooted and a shed and fence were damaged before the tornado lifted near Highway 129. [11/23/14: Tornado #9, County #2-2, EF0, Houston-Pulaski, 2014:026].

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 104 MPH, touched down in central Stewart County just southwest of the city of Lumpkin. The tornado tracked north northeast for less than a mile before lifting causing mainly damage to trees along Green Grove Road. [11/23/14: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Stewart, 2014:019].

The stage height on a USGS gage on the Allatoona Creek at Stilesboro Road near Mars Hill reached flood stage of 13 feet. The creek crest at 13.6 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields near the creek.

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 110 MPH, crossed the Chattahoochee River from Barbour County, Alabama into southwest Stewart County, Georgia southwest of the community of Coffington. The tornado tracked northeast for nearly 14 miles before lifting near the community of Julia along State Highway 39. The tornado mainly caused damage to trees with numerous hardwood and softwood trees either snapped or uprooted. [11/23/14: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Stewart, 2014:018].

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 107 MPH, touched down in Chattahoochee County around the town of Cusseta along U.S. Highway 27. The tornado tracked northeast around 18 miles mile before crossing into Marion County near County Road 65 and Little Juniper Creek. The tornado caused mainly damage to trees with numerous hardwood and softwood trees snapped or uprooted. [11/23/14: Tornado #3, County #1-3, EF1, Chattahoochee-Marion-Talbot, 2014:020].

A NWS storm survey team found that the EF-1 tornado that touched down in Chattahoochee County crossed the northwest corner of Marion County. The tornado crossed into Marion County near County Road 65 and traveled northeast for around one half mile before it crossed Upatoi Creek into Talbot County. Maximum wind speeds were around 100 MPH with mainly damage to trees. [11/23/14: Tornado #3, County #2-3, EF1, Chattahoochee-Marion-Talbot, 2014:020].

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 100 MPH, crossed Upatoi Creek from Marion County into Talbot County west of the Juniper community. The tornado tracked northeast around 2.5 miles mile before lifting around Benson Lake near the intersection of U.S. Highway 80 and the Cusseta Highway. The tornado caused mainly damage to trees with several hardwood and softwood trees snapped or uprooted. [11/23/14: Tornado #3, County #3-3, EF1, Chattahoochee-Marion-Talbot, 2014:020].

A NWS storm survey team found that an EF-2 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 130 MPH, touched down in Upson County on the west side of Thomaston around the intersection of State Highway 74 and W. Main Street. The tornado tracked northeast around 8.5 miles mile before crossing into Lamar County near north of Mud Bridge Road and Rocky bottom Road. Numerous hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted or snapped along the path of the tornado. The tornado reached its peak intensity northwest of Thomaston where it moved through a residential subdivision at Del Ray Road and Tyler Lane. A small residential leasing office was destroyed at this location with the exterior walls blown away. [11/23/14: Tornado #5, County #1-2, EF2, Upson-Lamar, 2014:022].

Numerous hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted or snapped along the path of the tornado. [11/23/14: Tornado #5, County #2-2, EF2, Upson-Lamar, 2014:022].

The emergency manager reported several small creeks and tributaries overflowing their banks in the upper reaches of the Euharlee Creek in southeast Polk County. Minor flooding of woodlands, fields and secondary roads occurred near the creeks.

The stage height on a USGS stream gage on the Euharlee Creek at US Highway 278 or West Elm Street in Rockmart reached flood stage of 9 feet. The creek crest at 10.5 feet. Minor flooding occurred in portions of the Wayside Park. Sections of the sidewalk along Water Street flooded.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Big Creek at Kimball Bridge Road near Alpharetta reached flood stage of 7 feet. The creek crest at 10.5 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields along the creek and portions of the Big Creek Greenway.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Little River at Old Georgia Highway 5 near Woodstock reached flood stage of 11 feet. The river crest at 12.9 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields along the river. A public boat ramp near the gage went under water. Low lying areas of the South Cherokee Recreation Park were flooded.

The stage height at a USGS stream gage on the Intrenchment Creek at Constitution Road around 6 miles southeast of Atlanta reached flood stage of 11 feet. The creek crest at 11.3 feet. Minor flooding of the woodlands and natural flood plain occurred along the creek.

A NWS survey team found thunderstorm wind damage in north DeKalb County. Damage was first noted to trees along Shallowford Road near the North Fork of Peachtree Creek. Several trees were downed along Cosmos Drive N.E. with some damage to homes due to falling limbs. A large tree was downed on a home on Hawthorne Place with several other trees down surrounding the home. Trees were also downed along Jasmine Court and Canna Ridge. Extensive tree and home damage was noted along Braithwood Road and Applewood Court where numerous trees were downed on homes. All damage noted to structures was due to falling trees or branches.

An NWS survey team found that a brief EF0 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 85 MPH and a maximum path width of 50 yards, touched down in far southern Pulaski County in the 1600 block of Pineview Highway. The tornado travelled .16 miles before dissipating. Approximately 20 small to medium-sized pine trees were snapped along the path of this tornado. A very large oak limb fell onto a brick outbuilding, causing minor damage to the roof and the covering was also blown off of a well house. [01/04/15: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF0, Pulaski, 2015:001].

An NWS survey team found that the same storm that produced a brief tornado in southern Pulaski County produced a new EF0 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 85 MPH and a maximum path width of 100 yards, in eastern Pulaski County. The tornado touched down on Raleigh Cobb Road and traveled east-northeast for 2.18 miles before dissipating near Midway Church Road and Fire Road 246. A tin covered barn was blown over and minor damage was noted to the roof of a home. Several trees were downed along the path of the tornado. [01/04/15: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF0, Pulaski, 2015:002].

An NWS survey team found that the same storm that produced two brief tornadoes in Pulaski County produced a brief EF1 tornado in central Dodge County. The tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 95 MPH and a maximum path width of 120 yards, touched down southwest of the intersection of Log Cabin Road and Antioch Church Road and traveled just 0.32 miles through the intersection before dissipating.  Around a dozen trees were downed narrowly missing homes and cars. [01/04/15: Tornado #3, County #1-1, EF1, Dodge, 2015:003].

The Brasstown RAWS site reported wind chill values below zero from around 6 PM EST on the evening of January 7th until around 8 AM EST on the morning of January 8th. The wind chill values remained below -10 degrees from around 9 PM EST on the 7th until after 7 AM EST on the 8th, bottoming out around 2 AM on the 8th when the air temperature of 1 degree combined with a 12 MPH wind to produce a wind chill of -16 degrees.

The Dawson County Emergency Manager reported approximately 50 trees blown down across the county from several hours of 30 to 35 MPH sustained winds with gusts estimated over 40 MPH. Several roads were blocked by downed trees and power outages were reported.
The ASOS at the Athens-Ben Epps Airport, KAHN, recorded a 51 MPH wind gust. No reports of damage were received from the several hours of strong winds in the county.

A Chattanooga Tennessee television news station reported a heat related death in Chickamauga, Georgia in Walker County. An 11-month-old boy was left in a closed vehicle for approximately two and a half hours during the afternoon of Saturday, September 5th. Air temperatures were reported to be in the lower 90s and a Walker County Sheriff's Department official estimated that temperatures inside of the vehicle reached as high as 130-170 degrees.

A NWS survey team determined that a tornado occurred in southern Telfair county. The EF1 tornado with estimated maximum winds around 94 MPH began along Raymond Bloodworth Barkley West Road between County roads 54 and 52 near China Hill and travelled 1.63 miles east northeast before ending along State Highway 117 near China Hill Road east of China Hill. The tornado snapped 15 to 20 hardwood trees and caused structural damage to a building lifting the roof off. No injuries were reported. [11/02/15: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Telfair, 2015:009].

A NWS survey team determined that a tornado occurred in southeastern Telfair county. The EF1 tornado with estimated maximum winds around 87 MPH began south of State Highway 134, west of Hugh McBride Road, and travelled .77 miles east northeast before ending along State Highway 134 east of Hugh McBride Road. The tornado snapped or uprooted numerous softwood and hardwood trees and caused structural damage to two center-pivot irrigation systems. No injuries were reported. The Telfair County 911 center reported a funnel cloud visible with this storm further east as it crossed U.S. Highway 341 north of Lumber City. Local law enforcement stopped traffic on the highway as the funnel cloud moved east, however they reported that there was no indication the circulation ever reached the ground and no damage was reported or found in this area. [11/02/15: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Telfair, 2015:010].

The Fulton County Emergency Manager reported a few trees blown down across Fulton County due to non-thunderstorm winds, including one tree down on Holly Road at Ezra Church Drive NW and another blocking lanes on Moreland Avenue SE. One man was killed when his vehicle struck a tree that had fallen across Woodhaven Road NW in the Buckhead area.

A local Atlanta television news station reported a man injured by a lightning strike near Meadow Lark after lightning struck a nearby power line and travelled through the ground to where the man was standing. The injuries were reported to be minor.

A NWS survey team found that a very short-lived EF1 tornado touched down in the Wynn Manor subdivision off of Tommy Lee Cook Road in northern Coweta County with maximum wind speeds around 105 MPH. The path length was less than a quarter of a mile; however the path width was around 200 yards at its maximum width. Structural damage occurred to at least five homes along George Wynn Road. The most significant damage was observed to a house on the corner of Lea Way and George Wynn Road where a portion of the roof and front porch were lifted and thrown nearly 50 yards away. Additional damage included fences blown over with 4��� X 4��� beams snapped near the base. Several small landscaping trees were snapped. [11/18/15: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF1, Coweta, 2015:011].

A NWS survey team found that a second EF1 tornado developed from the same thunderstorm that produced the earlier Coweta County tornado. This new tornado touched down near Creekside High School where minor damage occurred to the goal posts and bleachers at the football field. Around the Durham Lakes Country Club, several large pine trees were uprooted as the tornado became better organized. One minor injury was reported in this area when a tree fell on a car near the country club. Near the intersection of Virlyn B. Smith road and Dynasty Drive there was a 120-yard wide area where numerous large trees were snapped and uprooted around several homes. The homes sustained only very minor roof and/or siding damage; however there was a small, unsecured, shed that was ripped apart by the winds in this location. Along Tell Road, additional large trees, mainly pines, were snapped near their bases. |The tornado continued to move northeast snapping trees along Rivertown Road just north of Clarence Duncan Park. Along White Bird Way, which turns into Tall Deer Drive, trees were snapped and uprooted with several homes sustaining significant damage from falling trees. Similar damage was seen along Small Elk Court. Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be around 95 mph with a maximum width of 200 yards. The tornado rapidly weakened and lifted before reaching West Campbellton Street just north of the town of Fairburn. [11/18/15: Tornado #2, County #1-1, EF1, Fulton, 2015:012].

A NWS survey team determined that a very brief EF0 tornado touched down just northeast of the Mountain Industrial Blvd exit north of the Stone Mountain Pkwy near Tucker. Structural damage occurred at two locations along Hammermill Road. The front part of a north-facing wall was ripped apart at one location while across the street part of the roof and metal siding on the front of another building was peeled back. Just behind the first building, two pine trees were uprooted. Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 75 MPH. [11/18/15: Tornado #3, County #1-1, EF0, DeKalb, 2015:013].
The Gilmer Emergency Manager reported power lines blown down on Old Bucktown Road east of Ellijay.
The public reported multiple trees blown down along Iron Hill Cove in the Red Top Mountain State Park.

An NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-0 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 80 MPH and a maximum path width of 180 yards, touched down just west of Mt. Carmel Road and traveled .2 miles east northeast, crossing Mt. Carmel Road before lifting. Several trees were snapped or uprooted on either side of Mt. Carmel Road and a small shed was destroyed. [12/24/15: Tornado #1, County #1-1, EF0, Upson, [2015:014].
The public reported quarter sized hail in extreme northern Schley County.
An amateur radio operator reported multiple trees blown down.

The Emanuel County Fire Department reported a large pine tree and several smaller trees blown down, a metal dog house flattened and the skirting ripped from under a trailer as well as part of the roof lifted off of a restaurant in the Summertown area.

Rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches occurred in less than 12 hours over most of Gilmer County during the night and early morning hours. The heavy rain caused debris flows of mud which covered four roads and washed out four other roads. An additional 12 other roads were flooded for several hours. The flood waters from Cherry Log Creek surrounded three homes off of Joann Sisson Road which caused some evacuations. Water did not get into the three houses.

The USGS stream gauge on the Intrenchment Creek at Constitution Road reached flood stage of 11 feet. The creek crest at 11.1 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and natural flood plain of the creek upstream and downstream from the gauge.

A USGS stream gauge on Fausett Creek at Yukon Road near Talking Rock reached flood stage of 10 feet. Record flooding of 17.8 feet occurred in the woodlands and pastures along the creek upstream and downstream from the gauge. The water level hit the road bed around 4 feet above the culvert and erosion occurred to the embankments on the south side of road.  The old record was 17.0 feet on May 27, 1973.

A USGS stream gauge on the Talking Rock Creek just downstream from the merger of Scarecorn Creek and off of Patterson Road near Hinton reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 13.4 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands upstream and downstream from the gauge. Rapid flowing water caused dangerous erosion conditions to the banks.

A USGS stream gauge on the Cartecay River off Georgia Highway 52 near East Ellijay reached flood stage of 7 feet. The river had the second highest crest in its history at 11.1 feet. Major flooding occurred upstream and downstream from the gauge which affected around 15 townhouses and homes on Riverside Drive with at least one foot of water. Also a large portion of Maple Village Mobile Homes Park flooded near the merger of the river and Owltown Creek.

A USGS stream gauge on the Coosawattee River off Legion Road near Ellijay reached flood stage of 8 feet. The river crest at 13.9 feet. Major flooding affected around 45 homes and a few businesses in Ellijay with some evacuations. The Spring Ellijay Plant flooded and portions of the Pilgrims Pride Processing Plant parking lot were under 3 feet of water. The American Legion Post 82 building and the Georgia Power Substation next to the Post were flooded with around 3 feet of water. Most of the Harold Hefner River Park was flooded with a few feet of water.

A USGS stream gauge on the Little Tallapoosa River at Georgia Highway 100 near Bowden reached flood stage of 17 feet. The river crest at 18 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields along the river upstream and downstream from the gauge. Several roads and culverts were washed out on tributaries leading to the river between Bowden and Carrollton.
The public reported that a half inch of sleet had accumulated in the Chatsworth area by 1:00 PM EST.

The Gordon County Emergency Manager reported up to a half of an inch of sleet had accumulated in areas across the county by 1:30 PM EST. There were also reports from the public of up to a tenth of an inch of ice accumulation on trees and elevated surfaces from earlier freezing rain. A few automobile accidents were also attributed to icy roads across the county.

A USGS stream gauge on the Dog River at Bill Arp Road or Georgia Highway 5 near Fairplay reached flood stage of 13 feet. The river crest at 13.9 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and natural flood plain upstream and downstream from the gauge. Several roads and culverts were washed out on tributaries leading to the river.

A USGS stream gauge on the Sweetwater Creek near the Interstate 20 bridge near Austell reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 10.9 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and fields upstream and downstream from the gauge. Portions of a paintball playing field and athletic fields in the Woodrow Wilson Park on Mount Vernon Road flooded.
Several reports of 2 to 3 inches of snow were received from across Fannin County on social media, including in the Morganton and Blue Ridge areas.

A USGS stream gauge on North Fork Peachtree Creek at Buford Highway or Georgia Highway 13 near Atlanta reached flood stage of 13 feet. The creek crest at 14.8 feet. Significant flooding occurred upstream and downstream from the gauge. Large portions of the backyards of residential homes on Victory Drive...Dunwoody Place and Converse Drive flooded with around two feet of water. A portion of the Sun Tan Center parking lot near the gauge flooded. A few roads and culverts in the area were damaged or washed out.
A report of 4.8 inches of snow was received on social media from the Ella Gap area.
The Towns County Sheriff's Department reported 4 to 6 inches of snow across eastern portions of the county.

A USGS stream gauge on the South Fork Peachtree Creek at Johnson road near Atlanta reached flood stage of 13 feet. The creek crest at 13.9 feet. Minor flooding occurred upstream and downstream from the gauge Portions of backyards of residential homes on Noble Drive...Helen Drive and Kay Lane were flooded with around one foot of water. A few roads and culverts were damaged or washed out in the area.
A COOP observer reported 2 inches of snow 1 mile north northwest of Jasper. A report of 2.5 inches of snow was received from the Carns Mill area on social media.
A report of a quarter of an inch of ice accumulation from freezing rain in the Afton area was received on social media. A report of an inch of snow was received on social media in Dawsonville.

A USGS stream gauge on the Peachtree Creek at Northside Drive in Atlanta reached flood stage of 17 feet. The creek crest at 19.4 feet. Significant flooding occurred  upstream and downstream from the gauge. Parking lots near the section of Peachtree Road...Fairhaven Circle and Peachtree Memorial Drive began to flood. Woodward Way was completely flooded with several feet of water and around one foot of water was in some homes that have not been elevated. Sections of Sagamore Drive...Hanover West Drive...and Peachtree Battle Avenue and Circle were flooded with 1 to 4 feet of water. Around one foot of water was in some homes. Several evacuations were needed.

A USGS stream gauge on Nickajack Creek at Veterans Memorial Highway near Mableton reached flood stage of 10 feet. The creek crest at 11 feet. Minor flooding occurred in the woodlands and natural flood plain upstream and downstream from the gauge. Portions of Nickajack Park around one mile upstream from the gauge was flooded around one foot deep.

Several reports of 2 inches of snow were received from the White County Emergency Manager, a COOP observer, a CoCoRaHS observer, and on social media, in the Cleveland, Sautee and Helen areas. Trace amounts of sleet and freezing rain were also reported.

The Banks County Emergency Manager reported a quarter to a half of an inch of ice accumulation from freezing rain from Homer to Alto. One to three inches of snow was also reported in this area by the time the wintry weather ended.
